text:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।
text_kannada:
ಯಾ ನಿಶಾ ಸರ್ವಭೂತಾನಾಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗರ್ತಿ ಸಂಯಮೀ |
ಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗ್ರತಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಸಾ ನಿಶಾ ಪಶ್ಯತೋ ಮುನೇಃ || ೬೯ ||
text_telugu:
యా నిశా సర్వభూతానాం తస్యాం జాగర్తి సంయమీ |
యస్యాం జాగ్రతి భూతాని సా నిశా పశ్యతో మునేః || ౬౯ ||
transliteration:
yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ
translation_english: The self-restrained man stays awake during what is night for all creatures. That which creatures stay awake for, it is night to the discerning sage.
translation_kannada: ಎಲ್ಲ ಜೀವಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಯಾವುದು ರಾತ್ರಿಯೋ ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಯಮಿಯು ಎಚ್ಚರವಾಗಿರುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಯಾವುದರಲ್ಲಿ ಜೀವಿಗಳು ಎಚ್ಚರವಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆಯೋ ಅದು ಕಾಣುವ ಮುನಿಗೆ ರಾತ್ರಿ.
translation_telugu: అందరికి ఏది రాత్రియో, సంపూర్ణ నిగ్రహ వంతుడైన మహాత్ముడు ఆ స్థితిలో మేల్కొని ఉంటాడు. ఏ స్థితిలో ప్రాణులు ప్రాణులు మేల్కొని ఉంటారో జ్ఞాని అయిన మునికి అది రాత్రి.
context_english: yā—which; niśhā—night; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; tasyām—in that; jāgarti—is awake; sanyamī—self-controlled; yasyām—in which; jāgrati—are awake; bhūtāni—creatures; sā—that; niśhā—night; paśhyataḥ—see; muneḥ—sage
commentary_english: That which is real for the wordlyminded people is illusion for the sage? and vice versa. The sage lives in the Self. This is day for him. He is unconscious of the wordly phenomena. They are night for him? as it were. The ordinary man is unconscious of his real nature. Life in the spirit is night for him. He is experiencing the objects of sensual enjoyment. This is day for him. The Self is a nonentity for him For a sage this world is a nonentity.The wordlyminded people are in utter darkness as they have no knowledge of the Self. What is darkness for them is all light for the sage. The Self? Atman or Brahman is night for the worldlyminded persons. But the sage is fully awake. He is directly cognising the supreme Reality? the Light of lights. He is full of illumination and AtmaJnana or knowledge of the Self.

text:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं

समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।

तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे

स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।
text_kannada:
ಆಪೂರ್ಯಮಾಣಮಚಲಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಂ |
ಸಮುದ್ರಮಾಪಃ ಪ್ರವಿಶಂತಿ ಯದ್ವತ್ |
ತದ್ವತ್ಕಾಮಾ ಯಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶಂತಿ ಸರ್ವೇ |
ಸ ಶಾಂತಿಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ನ ಕಾಮಕಾಮೀ || ೭೦ ||
text_telugu:
ఆపూర్యమాణమచలప్రతిష్ఠం |
సముద్రమాపః ప్రవిశంతి యద్వత్ |
తద్వత్కామా యం ప్రవిశంతి సర్వే |
స శాంతిమాప్నోతి న కామకామీ || ౭౦ ||
transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ
samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve
sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
translation_english: That man attains peace into whom all desires enter, just as waters flow into the sea that remains unchanged even when filled from all sides. Not so one who is desirous of objects.
translation_kannada: ತುಂಬಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೂ ಅಚಲವಾಗಿ ನಿಂತಿರುವ ಸಮುದ್ರವನ್ನು ನೀರುಗಳು ಸೇರುವಂತೆ, ಯಾರೊಳಗೆ ಎಲ್ಲ ಬಯಕೆಗಳು ಸೇರಿ ಅಡಗುತ್ತವೆಯೋ ಅವನು ಶಾಂತಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಬಯಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬೆನ್ನಟ್ಟುವವನಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: పరిపూర్ణంగా స్థిరంగా నిలిచి ఉండే సముద్రాన్ని నీళ్ళు ఎలాచేరుకుంటాయో, ఎవరిలోకి అన్ని కోరికలు ప్రవేశించి విలీనమౌతాయో,అతడే శాంతిని పొందుతాడు. కోరికలకు దాసుడైనవాడు పొందలేడు.
context_english: āpūryamāṇam—filled from all sides; achala-pratiṣhṭham—undisturbed; samudram—ocean; āpaḥ—waters; praviśhanti—enter; yadvat—as; tadvat—likewise; kāmāḥ—desires; yam—whom; praviśhanti—enter; sarve—all; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—peace; āpnoti—attains; na—not; kāma-kāmī—one who strives to satisfy desires
commentary_english: Just as the ocean filled with waters from all sides remains unmoved? so also the sage who is resting in his own Svarupa or the Self is not a bit affected though desires of all sorts enter from all sides. The sage attains peace or liberation but not he who longs for objects of sensual enjoyment and entertains various desires. (Cf.XVIII.53?54).

text:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।
text_kannada:
ವಿಹಾಯ ಕಾಮಾನ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪುಮಾಂಶ್ಚರತಿ ನಿಃಸ್ಪೃಹಃ |
ನಿರ್ಮಮೋ ನಿರಹಂಕಾರಃ ಸ ಶಾಂತಿಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ || ೭೧ ||
text_telugu:
విహాయ కామాన్యః సర్వాన్పుమాంశ్చరతి నిఃస్పృహః |
నిర్మమో నిరహంకారః స శాంతిమధిగచ్ఛతి || ౭౧ ||
transliteration:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sa śhāntim adhigachchhati
translation_english: That man attains peace who, after rejecting all desires, moves about free from hankering, without the idea of 'me' and 'mine', and devoid of pride.
translation_kannada: ಎಲ್ಲ ಬಯಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ತೊರೆದು, ಆಸೆಯಿಲ್ಲದೆ, ನನ್ನದೆಂಬ ಭಾವವಿಲ್ಲದೆ, ಅಹಂಕಾರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ನಡೆಯುವ ಮನುಷ್ಯನು ಶಾಂತಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ.
translation_telugu: అన్ని కోరికలను వదిలి, అహంకార మమకారాలు వీడి సంచరించే పురుషుడు శాంతిని పొందుతాడు.
context_english: vihāya—giving up; kāmān—material desires; yaḥ—who; sarvān—all; pumān—a person; charati—lives; niḥspṛihaḥ—free from hankering; nirmamaḥ—without a sense of proprietorship; nirahankāraḥ—without egoism; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—perfect peace; adhigachchhati—attains
commentary_english: That man who lives destitute of longing? abandoning all desires? without the senses of I and mine? who is satisfied with the bare necessities of life? who does not care even for those bare necessities of life? who has no attachment even for the bare necessities of life? attains Moksha or eternal peace. (Cf.II.55).

text:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।
text_kannada:
ಏಷಾ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮೀ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನೈನಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ವಿಮುಹ್ಯತಿ |
ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾಽಸ್ಯಾಮಂತಕಾಲೇಽಪಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿರ್ವಾಣಮೃಚ್ಛತಿ || ೭೨ ||
text_telugu:
ఏషా బ్రాహ్మీ స్థితిః పార్థ నైనాం ప్రాప్య విముహ్యతి |
స్థిత్వాఽస్యామంతకాలేఽపి బ్రహ్మనిర్వాణమృచ్ఛతి || ౭౨ ||
transliteration:
eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛichchhati
translation_english: O Partha, this is the state of being established in Brahman. One does not become deluded after attaining this; one attains identification with Brahman by being established in this state even in the closing years of one's life.
translation_kannada: ಪಾರ್ಥನೇ, ಇದೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಲೆನಿಂತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ. ಇದನ್ನು ಪಡೆದವನು ಮತ್ತೆ ಮೋಹಗೊಳ್ಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಕೊನೆಗಾಲದಲ್ಲಾದರೂ ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಲೆನಿಂತವನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿರ್ವಾಣವನ್ನು ಸೇರುತ್ತಾನೆ.
translation_telugu: ఆర్జునా ఇదే బ్రాహ్మీస్థితి, దీనిని పొందాక ఇక భ్రమించడు. ఇందులో చివరి సమయంవరకు నిలిస్తే బ్రహ్మ నిర్వాణాన్ని పొందుతాడు.
context_english: eṣhā—such; brāhmī sthitiḥ—state of God-realization; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; na—never; enām—this; prāpya—having attained; vimuhyati—is deluded; sthitvā—being established; asyām—in this; anta-kāle—at the hour of death; api—even; brahma-nirvāṇam—liberation from Maya; ṛichchhati—attains
commentary_english: The state described in the previous verse -- to renounce everything and to live in Brahman -- is the Brahmic state or the state of Brahman. If one attains to this state one is never deluded. He attains Moksha if he stays in that state even at the hour of his death. It is needless to say that he who gets establised in Brahman throughout his life attains to the state of Brahman or,BrahmaNirvana (Cf.VIII.5?6).Maharshi Vidyaranya says in his Panchadasi that Antakala here means the moment at which Avidya or mutual superimposition of the Self and the notSelf ends.Thus in the Upanishads of the glorious Bhagavad Gita? the science of the Eternal? the scripture of Yoga? the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna? ends the second discourse entitledThe Sankhya Yoga.,

text:
अर्जुन उवाच

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।
text_kannada:
ಅರ್ಜುನ ಉವಾಚ |
ಜ್ಯಾಯಸೀ ಚೇತ್ಕರ್ಮಣಸ್ತೇ ಮತಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ಜನಾರ್ದನ |
ತತ್ಕಿಂ ಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಘೋರೇ ಮಾಂ ನಿಯೋಜಯಸಿ ಕೇಶವ || ೧ ||
text_telugu:
అర్జున ఉవాచ |
జ్యాయసీ చేత్కర్మణస్తే మతా బుద్ధిర్జనార్దన |
తత్కిం కర్మణి ఘోరే మాం నియోజయసి కేశవ || ౧ ||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśhava
translation_english: Arjuna said, "O Janardana (Krishna), if it is Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why do You urge me to take such horrible action, O Kesava?"
translation_kannada: ಅರ್ಜುನನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ಜನಾರ್ದನಾ, ಕರ್ಮಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಜ್ಞಾನವೇ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ ಎಂದು ನೀನು ಭಾವಿಸುವುದಾದರೆ, ಕೇಶವಾ, ಈ ಘೋರವಾದ ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಏಕೆ ತೊಡಗಿಸುತ್ತೀಯೆ?
translation_telugu: అర్జునుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు; జనార్ధనా! నీ అభిప్రాయంలో కర్మ కంటే జ్ఞానమే ఎక్కువైతే కేశవా! ఘోరకర్మలో నన్ను ఎందుకు నియోగించుతావు?
context_english: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; jyāyasī—superior; chet—if; karmaṇaḥ—than fruitive action; te—by you; matā—is considered; buddhiḥ—intellect; janārdana—he who looks after the public, Krishna; tat—then; kim—why; karmaṇi—action; ghore—terrible; mām—me; niyojayasi—do you engage; keśhava—Krishna, the killer of the demon named Keshi;
commentary_english: In verses 49? 50 and 51 of chapter II? Lord Krsihna has spoken very highly about Buddhi Yoga. He again asks Arjuna to fight. That is the reason why Arjuna is perplexed now.

text:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।

तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्।।3.2।।
text_kannada:
ವ್ಯಾಮಿಶ್ರೇಣೇವ ವಾಕ್ಯೇನ ಬುದ್ಧಿಂ ಮೋಹಯಸೀವ ಮೇ |
ತದೇಕಂ ವದ ನಿಶ್ಿಚತ್ಯ ಯೇನ ಶ್ರೇಯೋಽಹಮಾಪ್ನುಯಾಮ್ || ೨ ||
text_telugu:
వ్యామిశ్రేణేవ వాక్యేన బుద్ధిం మోహయసీవ మే |
తదేకం వద నిశ్ిచత్య యేన శ్రేయోఽహమాప్నుయామ్ || ౨ ||
transliteration:
vyāmiśhreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me
tad ekaṁ vada niśhchitya yena śhreyo ’ham āpnuyām
translation_english: You bewilder my understanding, as it were, with a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain which one of these I may use to attain the highest Good.
translation_kannada: ಒಗಟಿನಂತಿರುವ ಮಾತಿನಿಂದ ನನ್ನ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು ಗೊಂದಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸಿಲುಕಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವಂತಿದೆ. ಯಾವುದರಿಂದ ನಾನು ಒಳಿತನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತೇನೋ ಆ ಒಂದನ್ನು ನಿಶ್ಚಯಿಸಿ ಹೇಳು.
translation_telugu: అయోమయమైన మాటలతో నా బుద్ధికి భ్రాంతిని కలిగిస్తున్నావు.ఏది నాకు శ్రేయమో దానిని నిశ్చయముగా చెప్పు.
context_english: vyāmiśhreṇa iva—by your apparently ambiguous; vākyena—words; buddhim—intellect; mohayasi—I am getting bewildered; iva—as it were; me—my; tat—therefore; ekam—one; vada—please tell; niśhchitya—decisively; yena—by which; śhreyaḥ—the highest good; aham—I; āpnuyām—may attain
commentary_english: Arjuna says to Lord Krishna? Tecah me one of the two? knowledge or action? by which I may attain to the highest good or bliss or Moksha. (Cf.V.I).

text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।

ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्।।3.3।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರೀ ಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ |
ಲೋಕೇಽಸ್ಮಿಂದ್ವಿವಿಧಾ ನಿಷ್ಠಾ ಪುರಾ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಾ ಮಯಾನಘ |
ಜ್ಞಾನಯೋಗೇನ ಸಾಂಖ್ಯಾನಾಂ ಕರ್ಮಯೋಗೇನ ಯೋಗಿನಾಮ್ || ೩ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ |
లోకేఽస్మింద్వివిధా నిష్ఠా పురా ప్రోక్తా మయానఘ |
జ్ఞానయోగేన సాంఖ్యానాం కర్మయోగేన యోగినామ్ || ౩ ||
transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
loke’smin dvi-vidhā niṣhṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṁ karma-yogena yoginām
translation_english: The Blessed Lord said, O unblemished one, two kinds of steadfastness in this world were spoken of by Me in days gone by—through the Yoga of Knowledge for the men of realization; through the Yoga of Action for the yogis.
translation_kannada: ಶ್ರೀಭಗವಂತನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ಪಾಪರಹಿತನೇ, ಈ ಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡು ಬಗೆಯ ನಿಷ್ಠೆಯನ್ನು ನಾನು ಹಿಂದೆಯೇ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದೇನೆ. ಸಾಂಖ್ಯರಿಗೆ ಜ್ಞಾನಯೋಗದಿಂದ, ಯೋಗಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಕರ್ಮಯೋಗದಿಂದ.
translation_telugu: భగవంతుడు ఇలాపలికాడు; పాప రహితుడా ఈ లోకంలో సాంఖ్యులకు జ్ఞానయోగం చేతను యోగులకు కర్మయోగం చేతను సాధన, సృష్టికి ముందే నాచేత చెప్పబడినది.
context_english: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—the Blessed Lord said; loke—in the world; asmin—this; dvi-vidhā—two kinds of; niṣhṭhā—faith; purā—previously; proktā—explained; mayā—by me (Shree Krishna); anagha—sinless; jñāna-yogena—through the path of knowledge; sānkhyānām—for those inclined toward contemplation; karma-yogena—through the path of action; yoginām—of the yogis
commentary_english: The path of knowledge of the Sankhyas (Jnana Yoga) was described by Lord Krishna in chapter II? verses 11 to 38 the path of action (Karma Yoga) from 40 to 53.Pura Prokta may also mean In the beginning of creation the twofold path was given by Me to this world.Those who are endowed with the four means and who have sharp? subtle intellect and bold understanding are fit for Jnana Yoga. Those who have a tendency or inclination for wok are fit for Karma Yoga. (The four means are discrimination? dispassion? sixfold virutes? and longing for liberation. The sixfold virtues are control of the mind? control of the senses? fortitude (endurance)? turning away from the objects of the world? faith and tranillity.)It is not possible for a man to practise the two Yogas simultaneously. Karma Yoga is a means to an end. It purifies the heart and prepares the aspirant for the reception of knowledge. The Karma Yogi should take up Jnana Yoga as soon as his heart is purified. Jnana Yoga takes the aspirant directly to the goal without any extraneous help. (Cf.V.5).

text:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।

न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।।3.4।।
text_kannada:
ನ ಕರ್ಮಣಾಮನಾರಂಭಾನ್ನೈಷ್ಕರ್ಮ್ಯಂ ಪುರುಷೋಽಶ್ನುತೇ |
ನ ಚ ಸಂನ್ಯಸನಾದೇವ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಂ ಸಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ || ೪ ||
text_telugu:
న కర్మణామనారంభాన్నైష్కర్మ్యం పురుషోఽశ్నుతే |
న చ సంన్యసనాదేవ సిద్ధిం సమధిగచ్ఛతి || ౪ ||
transliteration:
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣhkarmyaṁ puruṣho ’śhnute
na cha sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigachchhati
translation_english: A person does not attain freedom from action by abstaining from action; nor does he attain fulfillment merely through renunciation.
translation_kannada: ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಆರಂಭಿಸದೆ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ಮನುಷ್ಯನು ಕರ್ಮಾತೀತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಕೇವಲ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ತೊರೆಯುವುದರಿಂದಲೂ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: కర్మలను చేయనంత మాత్రాన నిష్కర్మ సిద్ధి కలగదు.కేవలం సన్యసించడం వలన సరైన సిద్ధి కలగదు.
context_english: na—not; karmaṇām—of actions; anārambhāt—by abstaining from; naiṣhkarmyam—freedom from karmic reactions; puruṣhaḥ—a person; aśhnute—attains; na—not; cha—and; sannyasanāt—by renunciation; eva—only; siddhim—perfection; samadhigachchhati—attains
commentary_english: Actionlessness (Naishkarmyam) and perfection (Siddhi) are synonymous. The sage who has attained to perfection or reached the state of actionlessness rests in his own essential nature as ExistenceKnowledgeBliss Absolute (Satchidananda Svarupa). He has neither necessity nor desire for action as a means to an end. He has perfect satisfaction in the Self.One attains to the state of actionlessness by gaining the knowledge of the Self. If a man simply sits iet by abandoning action you cannot say that he has attained to the state of actionlessness. His mind will be planning? scheming and speculating. Thought is real action. The sage who is free from affirmative thoughts? wishes? and likes and dislikes? who has the knowledge of the Self can be said to have attained to the state of actionlessness.No one can reach perfection or freedom from action or knowledge of the Self by mere renunciation or by simply giving up activities without possessing the knowledge of the Self. (Cf.XVIII.49).

text:
न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।

कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।3.5।।
text_kannada:
ನ ಹಿ ಕಶ್ಿಚತ್ಕ್ಷಣಮಪಿ ಜಾತು ತಿಷ್ಠತ್ಯಕರ್ಮಕೃತ್ |
ಕಾರ್ಯತೇ ಹ್ಯವಶಃ ಕರ್ಮ ಸರ್ವಃ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಜೈರ್ಗುಣೈಃ || ೫ ||
text_telugu:
న హి కశ్ిచత్క్షణమపి జాతు తిష్ఠత్యకర్మకృత్ |
కార్యతే హ్యవశః కర్మ సర్వః ప్రకృతిజైర్గుణైః || ౫ ||
transliteration:
na hi kaśhchit kṣhaṇam api jātu tiṣhṭhatyakarma-kṛit
kāryate hyavaśhaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛiti-jair guṇaiḥ
translation_english: For no one ever remains even for a moment without doing work, for all are made to work under compulsion by the gunas born of Nature.
translation_kannada: ಯಾರೂ ಒಂದು ಕ್ಷಣವೂ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡದೆ ಇರಲಾರರು. ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯಿಂದ ಹುಟ್ಟಿದ ಗುಣಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲರಿಂದಲೂ ಬಲವಂತವಾಗಿ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.
translation_telugu: ఎవరూ ఒక్క క్షణం కూడా కర్మ చేయకుండా ఉండలేరు.ప్రకృతి జన్యమైన గుణాల వలన అన్ని కర్మలు అవశ్యంగానే చేయబడుతున్నాయి.
context_english: na—not; hi—certainly; kaśhchit—anyone; kṣhaṇam—a moment; api—even; jātu—ever; tiṣhṭhati—can remain; akarma-kṛit—without action; kāryate—are performed; hi—certainly; avaśhaḥ—helpless; karma—work; sarvaḥ—all; prakṛiti-jaiḥ—born of material nature; guṇaiḥ—by the qualities
commentary_english: The Gunas (alities of Nature) are three? viz.? Sattva? Rajas and Tamas. Sattva is harmony or light or purity Rajas is passion or motion Tamas is inertia or darkness. Sattvic actions help a man to attain to Moksha. Rajasic and Tamasic actions bind a man to Samsara.These alities cannot affect a man who has knowledge of the Self. He has crossed over these alities. He has become a Gunatita (one who has transcended the alities of Nature). The ignorant man who has no knowledge of the Self and who is swayed by Avidya or nescience is driven helplessly to action by the Gunas. (Cf.IV.16?XVIII.11).

text:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।

इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।3.6।।
text_kannada:
ಕರ್ಮೇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಸಂಯಮ್ಯ ಯ ಆಸ್ತೇ ಮನಸಾ ಸ್ಮರನ್ |
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾರ್ಥಾನ್ವಿಮೂಢಾತ್ಮಾ ಮಿಥ್ಯಾಚಾರಃ ಸ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ || ೬ ||
text_telugu:
కర్మేంద్రియాణి సంయమ్య య ఆస్తే మనసా స్మరన్ |
ఇంద్రియార్థాన్విమూఢాత్మా మిథ్యాచారః స ఉచ్యతే || ౬ ||
transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi sanyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyāchāraḥ sa uchyate
translation_english: One who, after withdrawing the organs of action, sits mentally recollecting the objects of the senses, is called a hypocrite, for they have a deluded mind.
translation_kannada: ಕರ್ಮೇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳನ್ನು ತಡೆಹಿಡಿದು, ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳ ವಿಷಯಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನೆಯುತ್ತಾ ಕುಳಿತಿರುವ ಮೂಢನನ್ನು ಮಿಥ್ಯಾಚಾರಿ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ.
translation_telugu: ఎవరైతే కర్మేంద్రియాలను నిగ్రహించి మనస్సులో ఇంద్రియ విషయాలను స్మరిస్తూ ఉంటాడో,అతడు పరమ మూర్ఖుడు,కపటాచారి అని పిలవ బడతాడు.
context_english: karma-indriyāṇi—the organs of action; sanyamya—restrain; yaḥ—who; āste—remain; manasā—in the mind; smaran—to remember; indriya-arthān—sense objects; vimūḍha-ātmā—the deluded; mithyā-āchāraḥ—hypocrite; saḥ—they; uchyate—are called
commentary_english: The five organs of action? Karma Indriyas? are Vak (organ of speech)? Pani (hands)? Padam (feet)? Upastha (genitals) and Guda (anus). They are born of the Rajasic portion of the five Tanmatras or subtle elements Vak from the Akasa Tanmatra (ether)? Pani from the Vayu Tanmatra (air)? Padam from the Agni Tanmatra (fire)? Upastha from the Apas Tanmatra (water)? and Guda from the Prithivi Tanmatra (earth). That man who? restraining the organs of action? sits revolving in his mind thoughts regarding the objects of the senses is a man of sinful conduct. He is selfdeluded. He is a veritable hypocrite.The organs of action must be controlled. The thoughts should also be controlled. The mind should be firmly fixed on the Lord. Only then will you become a true Yogi. Only then will you attain to Selfrealisation.

text:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।

कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।3.7।।
text_kannada:
ಯಸ್ತ್ವಿಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಮನಸಾ ನಿಯಮ್ಯಾರಭತೇಽರ್ಜುನ |
ಕರ್ಮೇಂದ್ರಿಯೈಃ ಕರ್ಮಯೋಗಮಸಕ್ತಃ ಸ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಯತೇ || ೭ ||
text_telugu:
యస్త్వింద్రియాణి మనసా నియమ్యారభతేఽర్జున |
కర్మేంద్రియైః కర్మయోగమసక్తః స విశిష్యతే || ౭ ||
transliteration:
yas tvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate ’rjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśhiṣhyate
translation_english: But, O Arjuna, one who engages in Karma-yoga, controlling the organs of action with the mind and becoming unattached, excels.
translation_kannada: ಅರ್ಜುನಾ, ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಿಂದ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳನ್ನು ಹತೋಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಂಡು, ಅಂಟಿಲ್ಲದವನಾಗಿ ಕರ್ಮೇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳಿಂದ ಕರ್ಮಯೋಗವನ್ನು ಆರಂಭಿಸುವವನೇ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ.
translation_telugu: అర్జునా;జ్ఞానేంద్రియాలను మనస్సు ద్వారా నిగ్రహించి,కర్మేంద్రియాల ద్వారా అసక్త భావంతో కర్మయోగాన్ని ఎవరు ప్రారంభిస్తాడో అతడు విశిష్టుడు అవుతాడు.
context_english: yaḥ—who; tu—but; indriyāṇi—the senses; manasā—by the mind; niyamya—control; ārabhate—begins; arjuna—Arjun; karma-indriyaiḥ—by the working senses; karma-yogam—karm yog; asaktaḥ—without attachment; saḥ—they; viśhiṣhyate—are superior
commentary_english: If anyone performs actions with his organs of action (viz.? hands? feet? organ of speech? etc.) controlling the organs of knowledge by the mind? and without expectation of the fruits of the actions and without egoism? he is certainly more worthy than the other who is a hypocrite or a man of false conduct. (Cf.II.64?68IV.21).The five organs of knowledge are the eyes? the ears? the nose? the skin and the sense of taste (tongue).

text:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।

शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।3.8।।
text_kannada:
ನಿಯತಂ ಕುರು ಕರ್ಮ ತ್ವಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಜ್ಯಾಯೋ ಹ್ಯಕರ್ಮಣಃ |
ಶರೀರಯಾತ್ರಾಪಿ ಚ ತೇ ನ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯೇದಕರ್ಮಣಃ || ೮ ||
text_telugu:
నియతం కురు కర్మ త్వం కర్మ జ్యాయో హ్యకర్మణః |
శరీరయాత్రాపి చ తే న ప్రసిద్ధ్యేదకర్మణః || ౮ ||
transliteration:
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śharīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
translation_english: You should perform your obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. Moreover, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible without action.
translation_kannada: ನಿನಗೆ ವಿಧಿಸಿದ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡು; ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡದಿರುವುದಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡುವುದೇ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ. ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡದಿದ್ದರೆ ನಿನ್ನ ದೇಹದ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆಯೂ ನಡೆಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: నీ విధ్యుక్త కర్మని నీవు చెయ్యి;కర్మ మానడం కంటే కర్మ చేయడం మేలు.కర్మ చేయకపోతే శరీర యాత్ర జరగదు.
context_english: niyatam—constantly; kuru—perform; karma—Vedic duties; tvam—you; karma—action; jyāyaḥ—superior; hi—certainly; akarmaṇaḥ—than inaction; śharīra—bodily; yātrā—maintenance; api—even; cha—and; te—your; na prasiddhyet—would not be possible; akarmaṇaḥ—inaction
commentary_english: Niyatam Karma is an obligatory duty which one is bound to perform. Thenonperformance of the bounden duties causes demerit. The performance of the obligatory duties is not a means for the attainment of a specific result. The performance does not cause any merit.Living itself involves several natural and unavoidable actions which have to be performed by all. It is ignorance to say? I can live doing nothing.

text:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।

तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।3.9।।
text_kannada:
ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಥಾತ್ಕರ್ಮಣೋಽನ್ಯತ್ರ ಲೋಕೋಽಯಂ ಕರ್ಮಬಂಧನಃ |
ತದರ್ಥಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಕೌಂತೇಯ ಮುಕ್ತಸಂಗಃ ಸಮಾಚರ || ೯ ||
text_telugu:
యజ్ఞార్థాత్కర్మణోఽన్యత్ర లోకోఽయం కర్మబంధనః |
తదర్థం కర్మ కౌంతేయ ముక్తసంగః సమాచర || ౯ ||
transliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samāchara
translation_english: This man becomes bound by actions other than those intended for God. Without being attached, O son of Kunti, perform actions for Him.
translation_kannada: ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುವ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಉಳಿದ ಕರ್ಮಗಳು ಈ ಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಂಧನವನ್ನುಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಕುಂತೀಪುತ್ರನೇ, ಆಸಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ತೊರೆದು ಯಜ್ಞಕ್ಕಾಗಿಯೇ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡು.
translation_telugu: కోసం చేసే కర్మలకంటే ఇతర కర్మలతో ఈ లోకం బంధింప బడి ఉన్నది.కుంతీకుమారా యజ్ఞ కర్మలనే సంగమము వదిలి కర్మలను చక్కగా చెయ్యి.
context_english: yajña-arthāt—for the sake of sacrifice; karmaṇaḥ—than action; anyatra—else; lokaḥ—material world; ayam—this; karma-bandhanaḥ—bondage through one’s work; tat—that; artham—for the sake of; karma—action; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; mukta-saṅgaḥ—free from attachment; samāchara—perform properly
commentary_english: Yajna means sacrifice or religious rite or any unselfish action done with a pure motive. It means also Isvara. The Taittiriya Samhita (of the Veda) says Yajna verily is Vishnu (174). If anyone does actions for the sake of the Lord? he is not bound. His heart is purified by performing actions for the sake of the Lord. Where this spirit of unselfishness does not govern the action? it will bind one to Samsara however good or glorious it may be. (Cf.II.48).

text:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्।।3.10।।
text_kannada:
ಸಹಯಜ್ಞಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಸೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ಪುರೋವಾಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ |
ಅನೇನ ಪ್ರಸವಿಷ್ಯಧ್ವಮೇಷ ವೋಽಸ್ತ್ವಿಷ್ಟಕಾಮಧುಕ್ || ೧೦ ||
text_telugu:
సహయజ్ఞాః ప్రజాః సృష్ట్వా పురోవాచ ప్రజాపతిః |
అనేన ప్రసవిష్యధ్వమేష వోఽస్త్విష్టకామధుక్ || ౧౦ ||
transliteration:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛiṣhṭvā purovācha prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣhyadhvam eṣha vo ’stviṣhṭa-kāma-dhuk
translation_english: In days of yore, having created the beings together with the sacrifices, Prajapati said, "By this, you shall multiply. Let this be your yielder of coveted objects of desire."
translation_kannada: ಹಿಂದೆ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಯು ಯಜ್ಞದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಿ ಹೇಳಿದನು. ಇದರಿಂದ ನೀವು ಬೆಳೆಯಿರಿ; ಇದೇ ನಿಮಗೆ ಬಯಸಿದ್ದನ್ನು ಕೊಡುವ ಕಾಮಧೇನುವಾಗಲಿ.
translation_telugu: యజ్ఞాలతో సహా ప్రజలను శృష్టించి ప్రజాపతి పూర్వం ఇలాచెప్పాడు.యజ్ఞం వలన మీరు వృద్ధి పొందండి.అది మీ ఇష్ట కామధేనువు.
context_english: saha—along with; yajñāḥ—sacrifices; prajāḥ—humankind; sṛiṣhṭvā—created; purā—in beginning; uvācha—said; prajā-patiḥ—Brahma; anena—by this; prasaviṣhyadhvam—increase prosperity; eṣhaḥ—these; vaḥ—your; astu—shall be; iṣhṭa-kāma-dhuk—bestower of all wishes
commentary_english: Prajapati is the Creator or Brahma. Kamadhuk is another name for the cow Kamadhenu. Kamadhenu is the cow of Indra from which everyone can milk whatever one desires. (Cf.VIII.4IX.2427X.25).

text:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।

परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।3.11।।
text_kannada:
ದೇವಾನ್ಭಾವಯತಾನೇನ ತೇ ದೇವಾ ಭಾವಯಂತು ವಃ |
ಪರಸ್ಪರಂ ಭಾವಯಂತಃ ಶ್ರೇಯಃ ಪರಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಥ || ೧೧ ||
text_telugu:
దేవాన్భావయతానేన తే దేవా భావయంతు వః |
పరస్పరం భావయంతః శ్రేయః పరమవాప్స్యథ || ౧౧ ||
transliteration:
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śhreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
translation_english: 'You nourish the gods with this. Let those gods nourish you in return. By mutually nourishing each other, you shall attain the supreme Good.'
translation_kannada: ಇದರಿಂದ ನೀವು ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪೋಷಿಸಿ, ಆ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ನಿಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಪೋಷಿಸಲಿ. ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಪೋಷಿಸುತ್ತಾ ನೀವು ಪರಮ ಒಳಿತನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುವಿರಿ.
translation_telugu: దేవతలను ఈ యజ్ఞంలో ఆరాధించండి.ఆదేవతలు మిమ్మలను అనుగ్రహిస్తారు.
context_english: devān—celestial gods; bhāvayatā—will be pleased; anena—by these (sacrifices); te—those; devāḥ—celestial gods; bhāvayantu—will be pleased; vaḥ—you; parasparam—one another; bhāvayantaḥ—pleasing one another; śhreyaḥ—prosperity; param—the supreme; avāpsyatha—shall achieve
commentary_english: Deva literally means the shining one. By this sacrifice you nourish the gods such as Indra. The gods shall nourish you with rain? etc. the highest good is the attainment of the knowledge of the Self which frees one from the round of births and deaths. The highest good may mean the attainment of heaven also. The fruit depends upon the motive of the aspirant.

text:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।
text_kannada:
ಇಷ್ಟಾನ್ಭೋಗಾನ್ಹಿ ವೋ ದೇವಾ ದಾಸ್ಯಂತೇ ಯಜ್ಞಭಾವಿತಾಃ |
ತೈರ್ದತ್ತಾನಪ್ರದಾಯೈಭ್ಯೋ ಯೋ ಭುಂಕ್ತೇ ಸ್ತೇನ ಏವ ಸಃ || ೧೨ ||
text_telugu:
ఇష్టాన్భోగాన్హి వో దేవా దాస్యంతే యజ్ఞభావితాః |
తైర్దత్తానప్రదాయైభ్యో యో భుంక్తే స్తేన ఏవ సః || ౧౨ ||
transliteration:
iṣhṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
translation_english: 'Being nourished by sacrifices, the gods will indeed give you the coveted enjoyments. He is certainly a thief who enjoys what has been given by them without offering it to them.'
translation_kannada: ಯಜ್ಞದಿಂದ ತೃಪ್ತರಾದ ದೇವತೆಗಳು ನಿಮಗೆ ಬೇಕಾದ ಭೋಗಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಡುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅವರು ಕೊಟ್ಟದ್ದನ್ನು ಅವರಿಗೆ ಅರ್ಪಿಸದೆ ತಾನೇ ಉಣ್ಣುವವನು ಕಳ್ಳನೇ ಸರಿ.
translation_telugu: యజ్ఞం చేత ఆరాధించబడిన దేవతలు మీకు ఇష్ట భోగాలను ఇస్తారు.వారికి ఏమీ సమర్పించకుండా వాళ్ళు ఇచ్చిన వాటిని అనిభవించేవాడు చోరుడే అవుతాడు .
context_english: iṣhṭān—desired; bhogān—necessities of life; hi—certainly; vaḥ—unto you; devāḥ—the celestial gods; dāsyante—will grant; yajña-bhāvitāḥ—satisfied by sacrifice; taiḥ—by them; dattān—things granted; apradāya—without offering; ebhyaḥ—to them; yaḥ—who; bhuṅkte—enjoys; stenaḥ—thieves; eva—verily; saḥ—they
commentary_english: When the gods are pleased with you sacrifices? they will bestow on you all the desired objects such as children? cattle? property? etc. He who enjoys what has been given to him by the gods? i.e.? he who gratifies the cravings of his own body and the senses without offering anything to the gods in return is a veritable thief. He is really a dacoit of the property of the gods.
translation_kannada_source: machine-assisted — rendered from the Sanskrit, no traditional Kannada edition

text:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।

भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।3.13।।
text_kannada:
ಯಜ್ಞಶಿಷ್ಟಾಶಿನಃ ಸಂತೋ ಮುಚ್ಯಂತೇ ಸರ್ವಕಿಲ್ಬಿಷೈಃ |
ಭುಂಜತೇ ತೇ ತ್ವಘಂ ಪಾಪಾ ಯೇ ಪಚಂತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕಾರಣಾತ್ || ೧೩ ||
text_telugu:
యజ్ఞశిష్టాశినః సంతో ముచ్యంతే సర్వకిల్బిషైః |
భుంజతే తే త్వఘం పాపా యే పచంత్యాత్మకారణాత్ || ౧౩ ||
transliteration:
yajña-śhiṣhṭāśhinaḥ santo muchyante sarva-kilbiṣhaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṁ pāpā ye pachantyātma-kāraṇāt
translation_english: By partaking in the remnants of sacrifices, they become freed from all sins. But those who are unholy and cook for themselves incur sin.
translation_kannada: ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಳಿದದ್ದನ್ನು ಉಣ್ಣುವ ಸಜ್ಜನರು ಎಲ್ಲ ಪಾಪಗಳಿಂದ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತಾರೆ. ತಮಗಾಗಿಯೇ ಅಡುಗೆ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ಪಾಪಿಗಳು ಪಾಪವನ್ನೇ ಉಣ್ಣುತ್ತಾರೆ.
translation_telugu: యజ్ఞంలో దేవతలకు ఇవ్వగా మిగిలినది తినేసజ్జనుడు అన్ని పాపాలనుండి విముక్తుడు అవుతాడు.తమ కోసం మాత్రం ఎవరు వండు కునే పాపాత్ములు వాళ్ళు పాపాన్నే తింటారు.
context_english: yajña-śhiṣhṭa—of remnants of food offered in sacrifice; aśhinaḥ—eaters; santaḥ—saintly persons; muchyante—are released; sarva—all kinds of; kilbiṣhaiḥ—from sins; bhuñjate—enjoy; te—they; tu—but; agham—sins; pāpāḥ—sinners; ye—who; pachanti—cook (food); ātma-kāraṇāt—for their own sake
commentary_english: Those who? after performing the five great sacrifices? eat the remnants of the food are freed from all the sins committed by these five agents of insect slaughter? viz.? (1) the pestle and mortar? (2) the grinding stone? (3) the fireplace? (4) the place where the waterpot is kept? and (5) the broom. These are the five places where injury to life is daily committed. The sins are washed away by the performance of the five MahaYajnas or great sacrifices which every Dvija(twicorn or the people belonging to the first three castes in Hindu society? especially the Brahmin) ought to perform1. DevaYajna Offering sacrifices to the gods which will satisfy them?2. BrahmaYajna or RishiYajna Teaching and reciting the scriptures which will satisfy Brahman and the Rishis?3. PitriYajna Offering libations of water to ones ancestors which will satisfy the manes?4. NriYajna The feeding of the hungry and the guests? and?5. BhutaYajna The feeding of the subhuman species? such as animals? birds? etc.

text:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।

यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।3.14।।
text_kannada:
ಅನ್ನಾದ್ಭವಂತಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಪರ್ಜನ್ಯಾದನ್ನಸಂಭವಃ |
ಯಜ್ಞಾದ್ಭವತಿ ಪರ್ಜನ್ಯೋ ಯಜ್ಞಃ ಕರ್ಮಸಮುದ್ಭವಃ || ೧೪ ||
text_telugu:
అన్నాద్భవంతి భూతాని పర్జన్యాదన్నసంభవః |
యజ్ఞాద్భవతి పర్జన్యో యజ్ఞః కర్మసముద్భవః || ౧౪ ||
transliteration:
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ
translation_english: From food are born the creatures; the origin of food is from rain; rain originates from sacrifice; sacrifice has action as its source.
translation_kannada: ಅನ್ನದಿಂದ ಜೀವಿಗಳು ಹುಟ್ಟುತ್ತವೆ, ಮಳೆಯಿಂದ ಅನ್ನವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಯಜ್ಞದಿಂದ ಮಳೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಯಜ್ಞವು ಕರ್ಮದಿಂದ ಹುಟ್ಟುತ್ತದೆ.
translation_telugu: అన్నము వలన జీవులు పుట్టును,అన్నము మేఘము వలన పుట్టును,మేఘము యజ్ఞము వలన పుట్టును,యజ్ఞము కర్మ వలననే సంబవము.
context_english: annāt—from food; bhavanti—subsist; bhūtāni—living beings; parjanyāt—from rains; anna—of food grains; sambhavaḥ—production; yajñāt—from the performance of sacrifice; bhavati—becomes possible; parjanyaḥ—rain; yajñaḥ—performance of sacrifice; karma—prescribed duties; samudbhavaḥ—born of
commentary_english: Here Yajna means Apurva or the subtle principle or the unseen form which a sacrifice assumes between the time of its performance and the time when its fruits manifest themselves.

text:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।

तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।3.15।।
text_kannada:
ಕರ್ಮ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೋದ್ಭವಂ ವಿದ್ಧಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾಕ್ಷರಸಮುದ್ಭವಮ್ |
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸರ್ವಗತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ನಿತ್ಯಂ ಯಜ್ಞೇ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಮ್ || ೧೫ ||
text_telugu:
కర్మ బ్రహ్మోద్భవం విద్ధి బ్రహ్మాక్షరసముద్భవమ్ |
తస్మాత్సర్వగతం బ్రహ్మ నిత్యం యజ్ఞే ప్రతిష్ఠితమ్ || ౧౫ ||
transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣhara-samudbhavam
tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣhṭhitam
translation_english: Know that action has the Vedas as its origin; the Vedas have the Immutable as their source. Hence, the all-pervading Vedas are forever based on sacrifice.
translation_kannada: ಕರ್ಮವು ವೇದದಿಂದ ಹುಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೆಂದೂ, ವೇದವು ಅಕ್ಷರವಾದ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮದಿಂದ ಹುಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೆಂದೂ ತಿಳಿ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಎಲ್ಲೆಡೆ ಇರುವ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವು ಸದಾ ಯಜ್ಞದಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಲೆಗೊಂಡಿದೆ.
translation_telugu: కర్మ బ్రహ్మదేవుని వలన జనించినది ఆ బ్రహ్మ అనంతమైన పరమాత్మ వలన ఉద్భవించాడు.కాబట్టి సర్వ వ్యాపకమగు పర బ్రహ్మము నిత్యమూ యజ్ఞములో ప్రతిష్టితమై ఉంటుందని తెలుసుకో.
context_english: karma—duties; brahma—in the Vedas; udbhavam—manifested; viddhi—you should know; brahma—The Vedas; akṣhara—from the Imperishable (God); samudbhavam—directly manifested; tasmāt—therefore; sarva-gatam—all-pervading; brahma—The Lord; nityam—eternally; yajñe—in sacrifice; pratiṣhṭhitam—established
commentary_english: Brahma may mean Veda. Just as the breath comes out of a man? so also the Veda is the breath of the Imperishable or the Omniscient. The Veda ever rests in the sacrifice? i.e.? it deals chiefly with sacrifices and the ways of their performance. (Cf.IV.24 to 32).Karma Action? Brahmodbhavam arisen from the injunctions of the Vedas.

text:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।

अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।
text_kannada:
ಏವಂ ಪ್ರವರ್ತಿತಂ ಚಕ್ರಂ ನಾನುವರ್ತಯತೀಹ ಯಃ |
ಅಘಾಯುರಿಂದ್ರಿಯಾರಾಮೋ ಮೋಘಂ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಸ ಜೀವತಿ || ೧೬ ||
text_telugu:
ఏవం ప్రవర్తితం చక్రం నానువర్తయతీహ యః |
అఘాయురింద్రియారామో మోఘం పార్థ స జీవతి || ౧౬ ||
transliteration:
evaṁ pravartitaṁ chakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
translation_english: O Partha, he who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion lives in vain, their life is sinful, and they indulge in the senses.
translation_kannada: ಪಾರ್ಥನೇ, ಹೀಗೆ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತಿರುವ ಚಕ್ರವನ್ನು ಈ ಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾರು ಅನುಸರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲವೋ, ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸುಖಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಳುಗಿದ ಆ ಪಾಪಿಯ ಬದುಕು ವ್ಯರ್ಥ.
translation_telugu: ఇలా పరిభ్రమించే చక్రాన్ని అనుసరించని వాడు పాపి,ఇంద్రియలోలుడు,అర్జునా;అతడు జీవించడం వ్యర్ధం.
context_english: evam—thus; pravartitam—set into motion; chakram—cycle; na—not; anuvartayati—follow; iha—in this life; yaḥ—who; agha-āyuḥ—sinful living; indriya-ārāmaḥ—for the delight of their senses; mogham—vainly; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; saḥ—they; jīvati—live
commentary_english: This is the wheel of action set in motion by the Creator on the basis of the Veda and sacrifice.He who does not follow the wheel by studying the Vedas and performing the sacrifices prescribed therein but who indulges only in sensual pleasures lives in vain. He is wasting his life. He is leading a worthless life indeed.One who does not live in accordance with this law and who is selfish commits sin. He violates the law of the Creator and that is the worst sin.

text:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।

आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।3.17।।
text_kannada:
ಯಸ್ತ್ವಾತ್ಮರತಿರೇವ ಸ್ಯಾದಾತ್ಮತೃಪ್ತಶ್ಚ ಮಾನವಃ |
ಆತ್ಮನ್ಯೇವ ಚ ಸಂತುಷ್ಟಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ || ೧೭ ||
text_telugu:
యస్త్వాత్మరతిరేవ స్యాదాత్మతృప్తశ్చ మానవః |
ఆత్మన్యేవ చ సంతుష్టస్తస్య కార్యం న విద్యతే || ౧౭ ||
transliteration:
yas tvātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛiptaśh cha mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva cha santuṣhṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate
translation_english: But that man who rejoices only in the Self, is satisfied with the Self, and is content only in the Self—for him there is no duty to perform.
translation_kannada: ಆದರೆ ಆತ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ರಮಿಸುವ, ಆತ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ತೃಪ್ತನಾದ, ಆತ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ಸಂತೋಷಗೊಂಡ ಮನುಷ್ಯನಿಗೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾದ ಕೆಲಸವೇನೂ ಉಳಿದಿಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: ఆత్మలోనే రమిస్తూ,ఆత్మలో తృప్తి పడుతూ,ఆత్మలోనే పరిపూర్ణ తృప్తిని పొందే వాడికి చేయదగిన కార్యమంటూ లేదు.
context_english: yaḥ—who; tu—but; ātma-ratiḥ—rejoice in the self; eva—certainly; syāt—is; ātma-tṛiptaḥ—self-satisfied; cha—and; mānavaḥ—human being; ātmani—in the self; eva—certainly; cha—and; santuṣhṭaḥ—satisfied; tasya—his; kāryam—duty; na—not; vidyate—exist
commentary_english: The sage does not depend on external objects for his happiness. He is ite satisfied with the Self. He finds his joy? bliss and contentment within his own Self. For such a sage who has knowledge of the Self? there is nothing to do. He has already done all actions. He has satisfied all his desires. He has complete satisfaction. (Cf.II.55).

text:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।

न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।
text_kannada:
ನೈವ ತಸ್ಯ ಕೃತೇನಾರ್ಥೋ ನಾಕೃತೇನೇಹ ಕಶ್ಚನ |
ನ ಚಾಸ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಭೂತೇಷು ಕಶ್ಿಚದರ್ಥವ್ಯಪಾಶ್ರಯಃ || ೧೮ ||
text_telugu:
నైవ తస్య కృతేనార్థో నాకృతేనేహ కశ్చన |
న చాస్య సర్వభూతేషు కశ్ిచదర్థవ్యపాశ్రయః || ౧౮ ||
transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛitenārtho nākṛiteneha kaśhchana
na chāsya sarva-bhūteṣhu kaśhchid artha-vyapāśhrayaḥ
translation_english: For him, there is no concern here at all with performing action, nor any with non-performance. Moreover, he has no dependence on any object to serve any purpose.
translation_kannada: ಅವನಿಗೆ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದಲೂ ಪ್ರಯೋಜನವಿಲ್ಲ, ಮಾಡದಿರುವುದರಿಂದಲೂ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಯಾವ ಜೀವಿಯನ್ನೂ ಅವನು ತನ್ನ ಪ್ರಯೋಜನಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಆಶ್ರಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: అతడికి పని చేయడం వలన ప్రయోజనం కాని ,మానడంవలన దోషం ఏమీ ఉండదు.తన ప్రయోజనం కోసం సమస్త ప్రాణులలోనూ దేనిపైనా ఆధారపడడు.
context_english: na—not; eva—indeed; tasya—his; kṛitena—by discharge of duty; arthaḥ—gain; na—not; akṛitena—without discharge of duty; iha—here; kaśhchana—whatsoever; na—never; cha—and; asya—of that person; sarva-bhūteṣhu—among all living beings; kaśhchit—any; artha—necessity; vyapāśhrayaḥ—to depend upon
commentary_english: The sage who is thus rejoicing in the Self does not gain anything by doing any action. For him really no purpose is served by an action. No evil (Pratyavaya Dosha) can touch him from inaction. He does not lose anything from inaction. He need not depend upon anybody to gain a particular object. He need not exert himself to get the favour of anybody.

text:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।

असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।3.19।।
text_kannada:
ತಸ್ಮಾದಸಕ್ತಃ ಸತತಂ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಸಮಾಚರ |
ಅಸಕ್ತೋ ಹ್ಯಾಚರನ್ಕರ್ಮ ಪರಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಪೂರುಷಃ || ೧೯ ||
text_telugu:
తస్మాదసక్తః సతతం కార్యం కర్మ సమాచర |
అసక్తో హ్యాచరన్కర్మ పరమాప్నోతి పూరుషః || ౧౯ ||
transliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara
asakto hyācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣhaḥ
translation_english: Therefore, remaining unattached, always perform the obligatory duty; for, by performing one's duty without attachment, a person attains the highest.
translation_kannada: ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಅಂಟಿಲ್ಲದವನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾದ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಸದಾ ಮಾಡು. ಅಂಟಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡುವ ಮನುಷ್ಯನು ಪರಮ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ.
translation_telugu: అందుచే కర్మఫలములందు ఆసక్తి లేనివాడై తన ధర్మముగా భావించి మానవుడు కర్మ నాచరింపవలెను. ఆసక్తి లేకుండ పనిచేయుటచే మానవుడు పరమసత్యమును పొందును.
context_english: tasmāt—therefore; asaktaḥ—without attachment; satatam—constantly; kāryam—duty; karma—action; samāchara—perform; asaktaḥ—unattached; hi—certainly; ācharan—performing; karma—work; param—the Supreme; āpnoti—attains; pūruṣhaḥ—a person
commentary_english: If you perform actions without attachment? for the sake of the Lord? you will attain to Selfrealisation through purity of heart. (Cf.II.64IV.19?23XVIII.49).

text:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।

लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।3.20।।
text_kannada:
ಕರ್ಮಣೈವ ಹಿ ಸಂಸಿದ್ಧಿಮಾಸ್ಥಿತಾ ಜನಕಾದಯಃ |
ಲೋಕಸಂಗ್ರಹಮೇವಾಪಿ ಸಂಪಶ್ಯನ್ಕರ್ತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ || ೨೦ ||
text_telugu:
కర్మణైవ హి సంసిద్ధిమాస్థితా జనకాదయః |
లోకసంగ్రహమేవాపి సంపశ్యన్కర్తుమర్హసి || ౨౦ ||
transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi sansiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśhyan kartum arhasi
translation_english: For Janaka and others strove to attain liberation through action itself. You should perform your duties, keeping in view the prevention of mankind from going astray.
translation_kannada: ಜನಕನೇ ಮೊದಲಾದವರು ಕರ್ಮದಿಂದಲೇ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು ಪಡೆದರು. ಲೋಕದ ಹಿತವನ್ನು ನೋಡಿಯಾದರೂ ನೀನು ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡಬೇಕು.
translation_telugu: జనకుడు మొదలైన వారు(నిస్కామ)కర్మల ద్వారానే మోక్షాన్ని పొందారు.లోకకల్యాణాన్ని దృష్టిలో ఉంచుకుని అయినా కర్మ చేయడమే నీకు తగును.
context_english: karmaṇā—by the performance of prescribed duties; eva—only; hi—certainly; sansiddhim—perfection; āsthitāḥ—attained; janaka-ādayaḥ—King Janak and other kings; loka-saṅgraham—for the welfare of the masses; eva api—only; sampaśhyan—considering; kartum—to perform; arhasi—you should;
commentary_english: Samsiddhi is Moksha (perfection or liberation). Janaka? (Asvapati) and others had perfect knowledge of the Self? and yet they performed actions in order to set an example to the masses. They worked for the guidance of men.

text:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।

स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।3.21।।
text_kannada:
ಯದ್ಯದಾಚರತಿ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠಸ್ತತ್ತದೇವೇತರೋ ಜನಃ |
ಸ ಯತ್ಪ್ರಮಾಣಂ ಕುರುತೇ ಲೋಕಸ್ತದನುವರ್ತತೇ || ೨೧ ||
text_telugu:
యద్యదాచరతి శ్రేష్ఠస్తత్తదేవేతరో జనః |
స యత్ప్రమాణం కురుతే లోకస్తదనువర్తతే || ౨౧ ||
transliteration:
yad yad ācharati śhreṣhṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
translation_english: Whatever a superior person does, another person does the same! Whatever they uphold as authority, an ordinary person follows that.
translation_kannada: ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠನಾದವನು ಏನೇನನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೋ ಅದನ್ನೇ ಉಳಿದ ಜನರೂ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅವನು ಯಾವುದನ್ನು ಮಾನದಂಡವಾಗಿಸುತ್ತಾನೋ ಲೋಕವು ಅದನ್ನೇ ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
translation_telugu: శ్రేష్టుడు దేనినైతే ఆచరిస్తాడో దానినే ఇతర జనులు ఆచరిస్తారు.అతడు దేనిని ప్రమాణంగా స్వీకరిస్తాడో దానినే లోకం అనుసరిస్తుంది.
context_english: yat yat—whatever; ācharati—does; śhreṣhṭhaḥ—the best; tat tat—that (alone); eva—certainly; itaraḥ—common; janaḥ—people; saḥ—they; yat—whichever; pramāṇam—standard; kurute—perform; lokaḥ—world; tat—that; anuvartate—pursues
commentary_english: Man is a social animal. He is an imitating animal too. He takes his ideas of right and wrong from those whom he regards as his moral superior. Whatever a great man follows? the same is considered as an authority by his followers. They try to follow him. They endeavour to walk in his footsteps.

text:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।

नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि।।3.22।।
text_kannada:
ನ ಮೇ ಪಾರ್ಥಾಸ್ತಿ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತ್ರಿಷು ಲೋಕೇಷು ಕಿಂಚನ |
ನಾನವಾಪ್ತಮವಾಪ್ತವ್ಯಂ ವರ್ತ ಏವ ಚ ಕರ್ಮಣಿ || ೨೨ ||
text_telugu:
న మే పార్థాస్తి కర్తవ్యం త్రిషు లోకేషు కించన |
నానవాప్తమవాప్తవ్యం వర్త ఏవ చ కర్మణి || ౨౨ ||
transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣhu lokeṣhu kiñchana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva cha karmaṇi
translation_english: In all the three worlds, O Partha, there is no duty for Me to fulfill; nothing remains unachieved or to be achieved. (Still,) I continue in action.
translation_kannada: ಪಾರ್ಥನೇ, ಮೂರು ಲೋಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ನಾನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾದ ಕೆಲಸವೇನೂ ಇಲ್ಲ; ಪಡೆಯಬೇಕಾದ್ದನ್ನೂ ಪಡೆಯದೆ ಉಳಿದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೂ ನಾನು ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿಯೇ ಇರುತ್ತೇನೆ.
translation_telugu: అర్జునా నాకు ఈ మూడు లోకాలలో చేయవలసిన పని లేదు.ఇంతకు ముందు పొందకుండా ఉన్నది ముందు పొందవలసినది ఏమీలేదు.అయిననూ కర్మలలో వర్తిస్తాను.
context_english: na—not; me—mine; pārtha—Arjun; asti—is; kartavyam—duty; triṣhu—in the three; lokeṣhu—worlds; kiñchana—any; na—not; anavāptam—to be attained; avāptavyam—to be gained; varte—I am engaged; eva—yet; cha—also; karmaṇi—in prescribed duties
commentary_english: I am the Lord of the universe and therefore I have no personal grounds to engage. Myself in action. I have nothing to achieve as I have all divine wealth? as the wealth of the universe is Mine? and yet I engage Myself in action.Why do you not follow My example Why do you not endeavour to prevent the masses from following the wrong path by setting an example yourself If you set an example? people will follow you as you are a leader with noble alities.

text:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।
text_kannada:
ಯದಿ ಹ್ಯಹಂ ನ ವರ್ತೇಯಂ ಜಾತು ಕರ್ಮಣ್ಯತಂದ್ರಿತಃ |
ಮಮ ವರ್ತ್ಮಾನುವರ್ತಂತೇ ಮನುಷ್ಯಾಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಸರ್ವಶಃ || ೨೩ ||
text_telugu:
యది హ్యహం న వర్తేయం జాతు కర్మణ్యతంద్రితః |
మమ వర్త్మానువర్తంతే మనుష్యాః పార్థ సర్వశః || ౨౩ ||
transliteration:
yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ
translation_english: For, O Partha, if at any time I do not continue vigilantly in action, people will follow My path in every way.
translation_kannada: ಪಾರ್ಥನೇ, ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ನಾನು ಎಚ್ಚರದಿಂದ ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗದಿದ್ದರೆ, ಮನುಷ್ಯರು ಎಲ್ಲ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ನನ್ನ ದಾರಿಯನ್ನೇ ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ.
translation_telugu: అర్జునా;నేను విశ్రాంతి లేకుండా నిరంతరం పని చేయకపోతే,మనుష్యులు అన్ని విధాల నామార్గమే అనుసరిస్తారు.
context_english: yadi—if; hi—certainly; aham—I; na—not; varteyam—thus engage; jātu—ever; karmaṇi—in the performance of prescribed duties; atandritaḥ—carefully; mama—my; vartma—path; anuvartante—follow; manuṣhyāḥ—all men; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; sarvaśhaḥ—in all respects
commentary_english: If I remain inactive? people also will imitate Me and keep iet. They will all become Tamasic and pass into a state of inertia.

text:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।

सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।3.24।।
text_kannada:
ಉತ್ಸೀದೇಯುರಿಮೇ ಲೋಕಾ ನ ಕುರ್ಯಾಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಚೇದಹಮ್ |
ಸಂಕರಸ್ಯ ಚ ಕರ್ತಾ ಸ್ಯಾಮುಪಹನ್ಯಾಮಿಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ || ೨೪ ||
text_telugu:
ఉత్సీదేయురిమే లోకా న కుర్యాం కర్మ చేదహమ్ |
సంకరస్య చ కర్తా స్యాముపహన్యామిమాః ప్రజాః || ౨౪ ||
transliteration:
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham
sankarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
translation_english: These worlds would be ruined if I did not perform action. And I shall become the agent of intermingling (of castes), and shall be destroying these beings.
translation_kannada: ನಾನು ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡದಿದ್ದರೆ ಈ ಲೋಕಗಳು ನಾಶವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ನಾನು ಸಂಕರಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣನಾಗಿ ಈ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕೆಡಿಸಿದಂತಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.
translation_telugu: నేను కర్మలు చేయకపోతే ఈలోకాలన్నీ నశించి పోతాయి.వర్ణ సంకరానికి కారకుడనౌతాను.ఈ ప్రజలను నాశనం చేసిన వాడనౌతాను.
context_english: utsīdeyuḥ—would perish; ime—all these; lokāḥ—worlds; na—not; kuryām—I perform; karma—prescribed duties; chet—if; aham—I; sankarasya—of uncultured population; cha—and; kartā—responsible; syām—would be; upahanyām—would destroy; imāḥ—all these; prajāḥ—living entities
commentary_english: If I did not engage in action? people would also be inactive. They would not do their duties according to the Varnasrama Dharma (code of morals governing their own order and stage of life). Hence confusion of castes would arise. I would have to destroy these beings.
translation_kannada_source: machine-assisted — rendered from the Sanskrit, no traditional Kannada edition

text:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।

कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्।।3.25।।
text_kannada:
ಸಕ್ತಾಃ ಕರ್ಮಣ್ಯವಿದ್ವಾಂಸೋ ಯಥಾ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಭಾರತ |
ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸ್ತಥಾಸಕ್ತಶ್ಿಚಕೀರ್ಷುರ್ಲೋಕಸಂಗ್ರಹಮ್ || ೨೫ ||
text_telugu:
సక్తాః కర్మణ్యవిద్వాంసో యథా కుర్వంతి భారత |
కుర్యాద్విద్వాంస్తథాసక్తశ్ిచకీర్షుర్లోకసంగ్రహమ్ || ౨౫ ||
transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvānso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāns tathāsaktaśh chikīrṣhur loka-saṅgraham
translation_english: O scion of the Bharata dynasty, as the unenlightened people act with attachment to work, so should the enlightened person act, without attachment, desiring to prevent people from going astray.
translation_kannada: ಭರತವಂಶದವನೇ, ತಿಳಿಯದವರು ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಟಿಕೊಂಡು ಹೇಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾರೋ, ಹಾಗೆಯೇ ತಿಳಿದವನು ಲೋಕದ ಹಿತವನ್ನು ಬಯಸಿ ಅಂಟಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಾಡಬೇಕು.
translation_telugu: అర్జునా;అజ్ఞానులు కర్మతో మునిగి తేలుతూ ఎలా పని చేస్తారో వివేకి లోక శ్రేయస్సు కోరుతూ అలాగే పని చేయాలి.
context_english: saktāḥ—attached; karmaṇi—duties; avidvānsaḥ—the ignorant; yathā—as much as; kurvanti—act; bhārata—scion of Bharat (Arjun); kuryāt—should do; vidvān—the wise; tathā—thus; asaktaḥ—unattached; chikīrṣhuḥ—wishing; loka-saṅgraham—welfare of the world
commentary_english: The ignorant man works in expectation of fruits. He says? I will do such and such work and will get such and such fruit. But the wise man who knows the Self? serves not for his own end. He should so act that the world? following his example? would attain peace? harmony? purity of heart? divine light and knowledge. A wise man is one who knows the Self. (Cf.II.64III.19XVIII.49).
translation_kannada_source: machine-assisted — rendered from the Sanskrit, no traditional Kannada edition

text:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।

जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्।।3.26।।
text_kannada:
ನ ಬುದ್ಧಿಭೇದಂ ಜನಯೇದಜ್ಞಾನಾಂ ಕರ್ಮಸಂಗಿನಾಮ್ |
ಜೋಷಯೇತ್ಸರ್ವಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ವಿದ್ವಾನ್ ಯುಕ್ತಃ ಸಮಾಚರನ್ || ೨೬ ||
text_telugu:
న బుద్ధిభేదం జనయేదజ్ఞానాం కర్మసంగినామ్ |
జోషయేత్సర్వకర్మాణి విద్వాన్ యుక్తః సమాచరన్ || ౨౬ ||
transliteration:
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām
joṣhayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācharan
translation_english: The enlightened man should not disturb the beliefs of the ignorant, who are attached to work. He should remain diligent himself and make them perform all their duties.
translation_kannada: ಕರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಟಿಕೊಂಡ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯನ್ನು ಕದಡಬಾರದು. ತಿಳಿದವನು ಯೋಗಿಯಾಗಿ ತಾನೇ ಎಲ್ಲ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾ ಅವರನ್ನೂ ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿಸಬೇಕು.
translation_telugu: కర్మలలో ఇరుక్కు పోయిన అజ్ఞానుల బుద్ధిని వివేకి చెదర కొట్టరాదు.తాను యోగంలో నిలిచి చక్కగా పని చేస్తూ వాళ్ళని ఆ మార్గంలో నడుస్తూ కర్మలాచరించేలా ప్రోత్సహించాలి.
context_english: na—not; buddhi-bhedam—discord in the intellects; janayet—should create; ajñānām—of the ignorant; karma-saṅginām—who are attached to fruitive actions; joṣhayet—should inspire (them) to perform; sarva—all; karmāṇi—prescribed; vidvān—the wise; yuktaḥ—enlightened; samācharan—performing properly
commentary_english: An ignorant may says to himelf? I shall do this action and thery enjoy its fruit. A wise man should not unsettle his belief. On the contrary he himself should set an example by performing his duties diligently but without attachment. The wise man should also persuade the ignorant never to neglect their duties. If need be? he should place before them in vivid colours the happiness they would enjoy here and hereafter by discharging such duties. When their hearts get purified in course of time? the wise man could sow the seeds of Karma Yoga (selfless service without deire) in them.

text:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।

अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते।।3.27।।
text_kannada:
ಪ್ರಕೃತೇಃ ಕ್ರಿಯಮಾಣಾನಿ ಗುಣೈಃ ಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ಸರ್ವಶಃ |
ಅಹಂಕಾರವಿಮೂಢಾತ್ಮಾ ಕರ್ತಾಽಹಮಿತಿ ಮನ್ಯತೇ || ೨೭ ||
text_telugu:
ప్రకృతేః క్రియమాణాని గుణైః కర్మాణి సర్వశః |
అహంకారవిమూఢాత్మా కర్తాఽహమితి మన్యతే || ౨౭ ||
transliteration:
prakṛiteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśhaḥ
ahankāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
translation_english: While actions are being done in every way by the gunas (qualities) of Nature, one who is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."
translation_kannada: ಎಲ್ಲ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನೂ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯ ಗುಣಗಳೇ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಆದರೆ ಅಹಂಕಾರದಿಂದ ಮೂಢನಾದವನು ನಾನೇ ಮಾಡುವವನು ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
translation_telugu: ప్రకృతి గుణాల వలన అన్ని కర్మలు నిర్వహింప బడతాయి.అహంకార వలన భ్రమించిన మూఢుడూ తానే కర్తనని తలపోస్తాడు.
context_english: prakṛiteḥ—of material nature; kriyamāṇāni—carried out; guṇaiḥ—by the three modes; karmāṇi—activities; sarvaśhaḥ—all kinds of; ahankāra-vimūḍha-ātmā—those who are bewildered by the ego and misidentify themselves with the body; kartā—the doer; aham—I; iti—thus; manyate—thinks
commentary_english: Prakriti or Pradhana or Nature is that state in which the three Gunas? viz.? Sattva? Rajas and Tamas exist in a state of eilibrium. When this eilibrium is disturbed? creation begins body? senses? mind? etc.? are formed. The man who is deluded by egoism identifies the Self with the body? mind? the life force and the senses and ascribes to the Self all the attributes of the body and the senses. He? therefore? thinks through ignorance? I am the doer. In reality the Gunas of Nature perform all actions. (Cf.III.29V.9IX.9?10XIII.21?24?30?32XVIII.13?14).

text:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।

गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते।।3.28।।
text_kannada:
ತತ್ತ್ವವಿತ್ತು ಮಹಾಬಾಹೋ ಗುಣಕರ್ಮವಿಭಾಗಯೋಃ |
ಗುಣಾ ಗುಣೇಷು ವರ್ತಂತ ಇತಿ ಮತ್ವಾ ನ ಸಜ್ಜತೇ || ೨೮ ||
text_telugu:
తత్త్వవిత్తు మహాబాహో గుణకర్మవిభాగయోః |
గుణా గుణేషు వర్తంత ఇతి మత్వా న సజ్జతే || ౨౮ ||
transliteration:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣhu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
translation_english: But, O mighty-armed one, the one who is a knower of the facts about the varieties of the gunas and actions does not become attached, thinking thus: 'The organs act on the objects of the organs.'
translation_kannada: ಮಹಾಬಾಹುವೇ, ಗುಣಗಳ ಮತ್ತು ಕರ್ಮಗಳ ವಿಭಾಗವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿದವನು, ಗುಣಗಳೇ ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿವೆ ಎಂದು ಅರಿತು ಅವುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಟಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
translation_telugu: మహాబలుడా;గుణకర్మ విభాగాల తత్వం తెలిసిన వాడుగుణాలు గూణాలలో వర్తిస్తాయని తెలిసి ఆ కర్మలలో తగుల్కోడు.
context_english: tattva-vit—the knower of the Truth; tu—but; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; guṇa-karma—from guṇas and karma; vibhāgayoḥ—distinguish; guṇāḥ—modes of material nature in the shape of the senses, mind, etc; guṇeṣhu—modes of material nature in the shape of objects of perception; vartante—are engaged; iti—thus; matvā—knowing; na—never; sajjate—becomes attached
commentary_english: He who knows the truth that the Self is entirely distinct from the three Gunas and actions does not become attached to the actions. He who knows the truth about the classification of the Gunas and their respective functions understands that the alities as senseorgans move amidst the alities as senseobjects. Therefore he is not attached to the actions. He knows? I am Akarta -- I am not the doer. (Cf.XIV.23).

text:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।3.29।।
text_kannada:
ಪ್ರಕೃತೇರ್ಗುಣಸಮ್ಮೂಢಾಃ ಸಜ್ಜಂತೇ ಗುಣಕರ್ಮಸು |
ತಾನಕೃತ್ಸ್ನವಿದೋ ಮಂದಾನ್ಕೃತ್ಸ್ನವಿನ್ನ ವಿಚಾಲಯೇತ್ || ೨೯ ||
text_telugu:
ప్రకృతేర్గుణసమ్మూఢాః సజ్జంతే గుణకర్మసు |
తానకృత్స్నవిదో మందాన్కృత్స్నవిన్న విచాలయేత్ || ౨౯ ||
transliteration:
prakṛiter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛitsna-vido mandān kṛitsna-vin na vichālayet
translation_english: Those who are completely deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The one who knows the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.
translation_kannada: ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯ ಗುಣಗಳಿಂದ ಮೋಹಗೊಂಡವರು ಗುಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಕರ್ಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಅಂಟಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಪೂರ್ತಿ ತಿಳಿಯದ ಆ ಮಂದಬುದ್ಧಿಗಳನ್ನು ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ತಿಳಿದವನು ಕದಡಬಾರದು.
translation_telugu: ప్రకృతి యొక్క గుణాల వలన మోహంలో పడిన వారు గుణ కర్మలలో మునుగుతుంటారు.సరిగా తెలియని మంద బుద్ధులను సర్వం తెలిసిన జ్ఞాని చెదర కొట్టరాదు.
context_english: prakṛiteḥ—of material nature; guṇa—by the modes of material nature; sammūḍhāḥ—deluded; sajjante—become attached; guṇa-karmasu—to results of actions; tān—those; akṛitsna-vidaḥ—persons without knowledge; mandān—the ignorant; kṛitsna-vit—persons with knowledge; na vichālayet—should not unsettle
commentary_english: The ignorant people do action with the expectation of fruits. The wise people who have the knowledge of the Self should not distract the faith or conviction or belief of such ignorant persons. If they unsettle their minds they will give up actions and become victims of inertia. They will lead an idle life. They should be encouraged by the wise to do actions of the Sakama type (actions for the sake of their fruits) in the beginning. The wise ones should turn the minds of the ignorant by giving them gradual instructions on Karma Yoga (Yoga of selfless? desireless action) and its benefits? viz.? purification of the heart that leads to the attainment of Selfrealisation.

text:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।

निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।3.30।।
text_kannada:
ಮಯಿ ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ಸಂನ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಚೇತಸಾ |
ನಿರಾಶೀರ್ನಿರ್ಮಮೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಯುಧ್ಯಸ್ವ ವಿಗತಜ್ವರಃ || ೩೦ ||
text_telugu:
మయి సర్వాణి కర్మాణి సంన్యస్యాధ్యాత్మచేతసా |
నిరాశీర్నిర్మమో భూత్వా యుధ్యస్వ విగతజ్వరః || ౩౦ ||
transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi sannyasyādhyātma-chetasā
nirāśhīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ
translation_english: Free from the fever of the soul, dedicate all actions to Me, with your mind intent on the Self, and become free from expectations and egoism, and engage in battle.
translation_kannada: ಎಲ್ಲ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನೂ ನನ್ನಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಪಿಸಿ, ಆತ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಮನಸ್ಸಿಟ್ಟು, ಆಸೆಯಿಲ್ಲದೆ, ನನ್ನದೆಂಬ ಭಾವವಿಲ್ಲದೆ, ಕಳವಳವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಯುದ್ಧ ಮಾಡು.
translation_telugu: సర్వ కర్మలను నాయందు సమర్పించి,చిత్తాన్ని ఆత్మలో నిలిపి,ఆశా మమకారాలను వదిలి,ఆరాటాన్ని విసర్జించి యుద్ధం చెయ్యి.
context_english: mayi—unto me; sarvāṇi—all; karmāṇi—works; sannyasya—renouncing completely; adhyātma-chetasā—with the thoughts resting on God; nirāśhīḥ—free from hankering for the results of the actions; nirmamaḥ—without ownership; bhūtvā—so being; yudhyasva—fight; vigata-jvaraḥ—without mental fever
commentary_english: Surrender all the actions to Me with the thought? I perform all actions for the sake of the Lord.Fever means grief? sorrow. (Cf.V.10XVIII.66).

text:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।

श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः।।3.31।।
text_kannada:
ಯೇ ಮೇ ಮತಮಿದಂ ನಿತ್ಯಮನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತಿ ಮಾನವಾಃ |
ಶ್ರದ್ಧಾವಂತೋಽನಸೂಯಂತೋ ಮುಚ್ಯಂತೇ ತೇಽಪಿ ಕರ್ಮಭಿಃ || ೩೧ ||
text_telugu:
యే మే మతమిదం నిత్యమనుతిష్ఠంతి మానవాః |
శ్రద్ధావంతోఽనసూయంతో ముచ్యంతే తేఽపి కర్మభిః || ౩౧ ||
transliteration:
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣhṭhanti mānavāḥ
śhraddhāvanto ’nasūyanto muchyante te ’pi karmabhiḥ
translation_english: Those who faithfully follow this teaching of Mine without cavil, they too become freed from their actions.
translation_kannada: ಶ್ರದ್ಧೆಯುಳ್ಳವರಾಗಿ, ದೋಷ ಹುಡುಕದೆ, ನನ್ನ ಈ ಮಾತನ್ನು ಸದಾ ಆಚರಿಸುವ ಮನುಷ್ಯರೂ ಕರ್ಮಗಳಿಂದ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತಾರೆ.
translation_telugu: నాయీ మతాన్ని ఏమానవులు మత్సరం లేకుండా ఆచరిస్తారో వాళ్ళు కూడా కర్మల నుండి విడుదల పొందుతారు.
context_english: ye—who; me—my; matam—teachings; idam—these; nityam—constantly; anutiṣhṭhanti—abide by; mānavāḥ—human beings; śhraddhā-vantaḥ—with profound faith; anasūyantaḥ—free from cavilling; muchyante—become free; te—those; api—also; karmabhiḥ—from the bondage of karma
commentary_english: Sraddha is a mental attitude. It means faith. It is faith in ones own Self? in the scriptures and in the teachings of the spiritual preceptor. It is compund of the higher emotion of faith? reverence and humility.

text:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।

सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः।।3.32।।
text_kannada:
ಯೇ ತ್ವೇತದಭ್ಯಸೂಯಂತೋ ನಾನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತಿ ಮೇ ಮತಮ್ |
ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಾನವಿಮೂಢಾಂಸ್ತಾನ್ವಿದ್ಧಿ ನಷ್ಟಾನಚೇತಸಃ || ೩೨ ||
text_telugu:
యే త్వేతదభ్యసూయంతో నానుతిష్ఠంతి మే మతమ్ |
సర్వజ్ఞానవిమూఢాంస్తాన్విద్ధి నష్టానచేతసః || ౩౨ ||
transliteration:
ye tvetad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣhṭhanti me matam
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāns tān viddhi naṣhṭān achetasaḥ
translation_english: But those who, finding fault where there is none, do not follow My teaching, know them—who are deluded about all knowledge concerning the qualified and the unqualified Brahman and who are devoid of discrimination—to have gone to ruin.
translation_kannada: ಆದರೆ ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ದೋಷ ಹುಡುಕುತ್ತಾ ನನ್ನ ಈ ಮಾತನ್ನು ಆಚರಿಸದವರನ್ನು, ಎಲ್ಲ ಜ್ಞಾನದಿಂದ ವಂಚಿತರಾದ, ವಿವೇಕವಿಲ್ಲದ, ಕೆಟ್ಟುಹೋದವರೆಂದು ತಿಳಿ.
translation_telugu: ఎవరైతే అసూయాపరులై నా ఈ మతాన్ని అనుష్టించరో ఆ తెలివితక్కువ వాళ్ళు సర్వ జ్ఞానములనుండి వంచితులై నశించిపోతారని తెలుసుకో.
context_english: ye—those; tu—but; etat—this; abhyasūyantaḥ—cavilling; na—not; anutiṣhṭhanti—follow; me—my; matam—teachings; sarva-jñāna—in all types of knowledge; vimūḍhān—deluded; tān—they are; viddhi—know; naṣhṭān—ruined; achetasaḥ—devoid of discrimination
commentary_english: The pigheaded people who are obstinate? who find fault with the teachings of the Lord and who do not practise them are certainly doomed to destruction. They are incorrigible and senseless persons indeed.

text:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।3.33।।
text_kannada:
ಸದೃಶಂ ಚೇಷ್ಟತೇ ಸ್ವಸ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಕೃತೇರ್ಜ್ಞಾನವಾನಪಿ |
ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಂ ಯಾಂತಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ನಿಗ್ರಹಃ ಕಿಂ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ || ೩೩ ||
text_telugu:
సదృశం చేష్టతే స్వస్యాః ప్రకృతేర్జ్ఞానవానపి |
ప్రకృతిం యాంతి భూతాని నిగ్రహః కిం కరిష్యతి || ౩౩ ||
transliteration:
sadṛiśhaṁ cheṣhṭate svasyāḥ prakṛiter jñānavān api
prakṛitiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣhyati
translation_english: Even a man of wisdom behaves according to his own nature. They follow their nature. What can restraint do?
translation_kannada: ಜ್ಞಾನಿಯಾದವನೂ ತನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಗೆ ತಕ್ಕಂತೆಯೇ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಜೀವಿಗಳು ತಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯನ್ನೇ ಹಿಂಬಾಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಬಲವಂತದ ನಿಗ್ರಹ ಏನು ಮಾಡೀತು?
translation_telugu: జ్ఞానవంతుడైనా తన ప్రకృతి ననుసరించే వ్యవహరిస్తాడు.ప్రాణులు తమ ప్రకృతిని అనుసరిస్తాయి.నిగ్రహమేమి చేస్తుంది.
context_english: sadṛiśham—accordingly; cheṣhṭate—act; svasyāḥ—by their own; prakṛiteḥ—modes of nature; jñāna-vān—the wise; api—even; prakṛitim—nature; yānti—follow; bhūtāni—all living beings; nigrahaḥ—repression; kim—what; kariṣhyati—will do
commentary_english: He who reads this verse will come to the conclusion that there is no scope for mans personal exertion. It is not so. Read the following verse. It clearly indicates that man can coner Nature if he rises above the sway of RagaDvesha (love and hatred).The passionate and ignorant man only comes under the sway of his natural propensities? and his lower nature. He cannot have any restraint over the senses and the two currents of likes and dislikes. The seeker after Truth who is endowed with the four means? and who is constantly practising meditation can easily control Nature. (Cf.II.60V.14XVIII.59).

text:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।

तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ।।3.34।।
text_kannada:
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸ್ಯೇಂದ್ರಿಯಸ್ಯಾರ್ಥೇ ರಾಗದ್ವೇಷೌ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತೌ |
ತಯೋರ್ನ ವಶಮಾಗಚ್ಛೇತ್ತೌ ಹ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪರಿಪಂಥಿನೌ || ೩೪ ||
text_telugu:
ఇంద్రియస్యేంద్రియస్యార్థే రాగద్వేషౌ వ్యవస్థితౌ |
తయోర్న వశమాగచ్ఛేత్తౌ హ్యస్య పరిపంథినౌ || ౩౪ ||
transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣhau vyavasthitau
tayor na vaśham āgachchhet tau hyasya paripanthinau
translation_english: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with respect to the objects of all the organs. One should not be swayed by these two, as they are adversaries.
translation_kannada: ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಕ್ಕೂ ಅದರ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ರಾಗ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ವೇಷ ನೆಲೆಸಿವೆ. ಅವುಗಳ ವಶಕ್ಕೆ ಒಳಗಾಗಬಾರದು; ಅವೆರಡೂ ದಾರಿಗೆ ಅಡ್ಡಿಯಾದ ಶತ್ರುಗಳು.
translation_telugu: ప్రతి ఇంద్రియ విషయంలోను రాగాద్వేషాలు ఉంటాయి కర్మయోగి వాటికి లోబడ రాదు.అవే అతనికి శత్రువులు.
context_english: indriyasya—of the senses; indriyasya arthe—in the sense objects; rāga—attachment; dveṣhau—aversion; vyavasthitau—situated; tayoḥ—of them; na—never; vaśham—be controlled; āgachchhet—should become; tau—those; hi—certainly; asya—for him; paripanthinau—foes
commentary_english: Each sense has got attraction for a pleasant object and aversion for a disagreeable object. If one can control these two currents? viz.? attachment and aversion? he will not come under the sway of these two currents. Here lies the scope for personal exertion or Purushartha. Nature which contains the sum total of ones Samskaras or the latent selfproductive impressions of the past actions of merit and demerit draws a man to its course through the two currents? attachment and aversion. If one can control these two currents? if he can rise above the sway of love and hate through discrimination and Vichara or right eniry? he can coner Nature and attain immortality and eternal bliss. He willl no longer be subject to his own nature now. One should always exert to free himself from attachment and aversion to the objects of the senses.

text:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।

स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.35।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರೇಯಾನ್ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮೋ ವಿಗುಣಃ ಪರಧರ್ಮಾತ್ಸ್ವನುಷ್ಠಿತಾತ್ |
ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮೇ ನಿಧನಂ ಶ್ರೇಯಃ ಪರಧರ್ಮೋ ಭಯಾವಹಃ || ೩೫ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రేయాన్స్వధర్మో విగుణః పరధర్మాత్స్వనుష్ఠితాత్ |
స్వధర్మే నిధనం శ్రేయః పరధర్మో భయావహః || ౩౫ ||
transliteration:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
swa-dharme nidhanaṁ śhreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ
translation_english: One's own duty, though defective, is superior to another's duty well-performed. Death is better while engaged in one's own duty; another's duty is full of fear.
translation_kannada: ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಆಚರಿಸಿದ ಪರಧರ್ಮಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಗುಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೂ ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮವೇ ಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠ. ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾವು ಬಂದರೂ ಒಳಿತು; ಪರಧರ್ಮವು ಭಯವನ್ನು ತರುತ್ತದೆ.
translation_telugu: బాగా ఆచరించిన పర ధర్మం కన్నా లోపభూయిష్టమైనది ఐనా స్వధర్మం మేలు.పర ధర్మం భయంకర మైనది.
context_english: śhreyān—better; swa-dharmaḥ—personal duty; viguṇaḥ—tinged with faults; para-dharmāt—than another’s prescribed duties; su-anuṣhṭhitāt—perfectly done; swa-dharme—in one’s personal duties; nidhanam—death; śhreyaḥ—better; para-dharmaḥ—duties prescribed for others; bhaya-āvahaḥ—fraught with fear
commentary_english: It is indeed better for man to die discharging his own duty though destitute of merit than for him to live doing the duty of another though performed in a perfect manner. For the duty of another has its pitfalls. The duty of a Kshatriya is to fight in a righteous battle. Arjuna must fight. This is his duty. Even if he dies in the discharge of his own duty? it is better for him. He will go to heaven. He should not do the duty of another man. This will bring him peril. He should not stop from fighting and enter the path of renunciation. (Cf.XVIII.47).

text:
अर्जुन उवाच

अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।

अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।
text_kannada:
ಅರ್ಜುನ ಉವಾಚ |
ಅಥ ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಯುಕ್ತೋಽಯಂ ಪಾಪಂ ಚರತಿ ಪೂರುಷಃ |
ಅನಿಚ್ಛನ್ನಪಿ ವಾರ್ಷ್ಣೇಯ ಬಲಾದಿವ ನಿಯೋಜಿತಃ || ೩೬ ||
text_telugu:
అర్జున ఉవాచ |
అథ కేన ప్రయుక్తోఽయం పాపం చరతి పూరుషః |
అనిచ్ఛన్నపి వార్ష్ణేయ బలాదివ నియోజితః || ౩౬ ||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpaṁ charati pūruṣhaḥ
anichchhann api vārṣhṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
translation_english: Arjuna said, "Now then, O scion of the Vrsni dynasty (Krsna), what compels this man to commit sin even against his will, as if he were constrained by force?"
translation_kannada: ಅರ್ಜುನನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ವೃಷ್ಣಿವಂಶದವನೇ, ಇಷ್ಟವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಬಲವಂತವಾಗಿ ತಳ್ಳಲ್ಪಟ್ಟವನಂತೆ ಮನುಷ್ಯನು ಯಾವುದರ ಪ್ರೇರಣೆಯಿಂದ ಪಾಪವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ?
translation_telugu: అర్జునుడు ఇలాఅడిగాడు; కృష్ణా ఇష్టం లేకపోయినా ఎవరో బలవంత పెడుతున్నట్లు మానవుడు పాపం ఎందుకు చేస్తున్నాడు?ఆ ప్రేరణశక్తి ఎవరిది?ఎవరి కారణంగా పాపం చేస్తాడు?

commentary_english: Varshneya is one born in the family of the Vrishnis? a name of Krishna.

text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।

महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्।।3.37।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರೀ ಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ |
ಕಾಮ ಏಷ ಕ್ರೋಧ ಏಷ ರಜೋಗುಣಸಮುದ್ಭವಃ |
ಮಹಾಶನೋ ಮಹಾಪಾಪ್ಮಾ ವಿದ್ಧ್ಯೇನಮಿಹ ವೈರಿಣಮ್ || ೩೭ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ |
కామ ఏష క్రోధ ఏష రజోగుణసముద్భవః |
మహాశనో మహాపాప్మా విద్ధ్యేనమిహ వైరిణమ్ || ౩౭ ||

śhrī bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣha krodha eṣha rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśhano mahā-pāpmā viddhyenam iha vairiṇam
translation_english: The Blessed Lord said, "This desire, this anger, born of the quality of rajas, is a great devourer, a great source of sin. Know this to be the enemy here."
translation_kannada: ಶ್ರೀಭಗವಂತನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ರಜೋಗುಣದಿಂದ ಹುಟ್ಟಿದ ಈ ಬಯಕೆಯೇ, ಇದೇ ಕೋಪವಾಗಿ ಮಾರ್ಪಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದು ಎಂದೂ ತೃಪ್ತಿಯಾಗದ್ದು, ಬಹಳ ಪಾಪ ಮಾಡಿಸುವಂಥದ್ದು; ಇದನ್ನೇ ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಶತ್ರು ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿ.
translation_telugu: శ్రీ భగవానుడన్నాడు; ఇవి కామము,క్రోధము,రజోగుణం నుండి ఉద్భవిస్తాయి.దానికి మహా ఆకలి.అది పాపిష్టిది.ఈలోకంలో అందరికి అదేశత్రువని తెలుసుకో.
context_english: śhri-bhagavān uvācha—the Supreme Lord said; kāmaḥ—desire; eṣhaḥ—this; krodhaḥ—wrath; eṣhaḥ—this; rajaḥ-guṇa—the mode of passion; samudbhavaḥ—born of; mahā-aśhanaḥ—all-devouring; mahā-pāpmā—greatly sinful; viddhi—know; enam—this; iha—in the material world; vairiṇam—the enemy
commentary_english: Bhagavan Bhaga means the six attributes? viz.? Jnana (knowledge)? Vairagya (dispassion)? Kirti (fame)? Aishvarya (divine manifestations and excellences)? Sri (wealth)? and Bala (might). He who possesses these six attributes and who has a perfect knowledge of the origin and the end of the universe is Bhagavan or the Lord.The cause of all sin and wrong action in this world is desire. Anger is desire itself. When a desire is not gratified? the man becomes angry against those who stand as obstacles on the path of fulfilment.The desire is born of the ality of Rajas. When desire arises? it generates Rajas and urges the man to work in order to possess the object. Therefore? know that this desire is mans foe on this earth. (Cf.XVI.21).

धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च।

यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्।।3.38।।
text_kannada:
ಧೂಮೇನಾವ್ರಿಯತೇ ವಹ್ನಿರ್ಯಥಾಽಽದರ್ಶೋ ಮಲೇನ ಚ |
ಯಥೋಲ್ಬೇನಾವೃತೋ ಗರ್ಭಸ್ತಥಾ ತೇನೇದಮಾವೃತಮ್ || ೩೮ ||

యథోల్బేనావృతో గర్భస్తథా తేనేదమావృతమ్ || ౩౮ ||

yatholbenāvṛito garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛitam

text:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।

कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।
text_kannada:
ಆವೃತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಮೇತೇನ ಜ್ಞಾನಿನೋ ನಿತ್ಯವೈರಿಣಾ |
ಕಾಮರೂಪೇಣ ಕೌಂತೇಯ ದುಷ್ಪೂರೇಣಾನಲೇನ ಚ || ೩೯ ||
text_telugu:
ఆవృతం జ్ఞానమేతేన జ్ఞానినో నిత్యవైరిణా |
కామరూపేణ కౌంతేయ దుష్పూరేణానలేన చ || ౩౯ ||
transliteration:
āvṛitaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣhpūreṇānalena cha
translation_english: O son of Kunti, knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, which is an insatiable fire.
translation_kannada: ಕುಂತೀಪುತ್ರನೇ, ಎಂದೂ ತುಂಬಲಾಗದ ಬೆಂಕಿಯಂತಿರುವ, ಬಯಕೆಯ ರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಈ ನಿತ್ಯಶತ್ರುವಿನಿಂದ ಜ್ಞಾನಿಯ ಜ್ಞಾನವು ಮುಚ್ಚಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಿದೆ.
translation_telugu: కామం తృప్తి పరచడానికి వీలులేని అగ్ని వంటిది.ఇది జ్ఞానానికి నిత్య శత్రువు.దీనితోజ్ఞాని జ్ఞానం కప్పబడి ఉంటుంది.
context_english: āvṛitam—covered; jñānam—knowledge; etena—by this; jñāninaḥ—of the wise; nitya-vairiṇā—by the perpetual enemy; kāma-rūpeṇa—in the form of desires; kaunteya—Arjun the son of Kunti; duṣhpūreṇa—insatiable; analena—like fire; cha—and
commentary_english: Manu says? Desire can never be satiated or cooled down by the enjoyment ofobjects. But as fire blazes forth the more when fed with Ghee (melted butter) and wood? so it grows the more it feeds on the objects of enjoyment. If all the foodstuffs of the earth? all the precious metals? all the animals and all the beautiful women were to pass into the possession of one man endowed with desire? they would still fail to give him satisfaction.The ignorant man considers desire as his friend when he craves for objects. He welcomes desire for the gratification of the senses but the wise man knows from experience even before suffering the conseence that desire will bring only troubles and misery for him. So it is a constant enemy of the wise but not of the ignorant.

text:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।

एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।
text_kannada:
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಮನೋ ಬುದ್ಧಿರಸ್ಯಾಧಿಷ್ಠಾನಮುಚ್ಯತೇ |
ಏತೈರ್ವಿಮೋಹಯತ್ಯೇಷ ಜ್ಞಾನಮಾವೃತ್ಯ ದೇಹಿನಮ್ || ೪೦ ||
text_telugu:
ఇంద్రియాణి మనో బుద్ధిరస్యాధిష్ఠానముచ్యతే |
ఏతైర్విమోహయత్యేష జ్ఞానమావృత్య దేహినమ్ || ౪౦ ||
transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣhṭhānam uchyate
etair vimohayatyeṣha jñānam āvṛitya dehinam

translation_kannada: ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳು, ಮನಸ್ಸು ಮತ್ತು ಬುದ್ಧಿ ಇವು ಇದರ ನೆಲೆ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಇವುಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಇದು ಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನು ಮುಚ್ಚಿ ದೇಹಧಾರಿಯನ್ನು ಮೋಹಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
translation_telugu: ఇంద్రియాలు మనస్సు,భుద్ధి,కామానికి ఆధార స్థానాలు అని చెప్పబడుతున్నాయి.ఈ కామం జ్ఞానాన్ని కప్పి వేసి ఇంద్రియాల ద్వారా దేహధారిని వ్యామోహ పరుస్తుంది.
context_english: indriyāṇi—the senses; manaḥ—the mind; buddhiḥ—the intellect; asya—of this; adhiṣhṭhānam—dwelling place; uchyate—are said to be; etaiḥ—by these; vimohayati—deludes; eṣhaḥ—this; jñānam—knowledge; āvṛitya—clouds; dehinam—the embodied soul
commentary_english: If the abode of the enemy is known it is ite easy to kill him. So Lord Krishna like a wise army general points out to Arjuna the abode of desire so that he may be able to attack it and kill it ite readily.

text:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।

पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्।।3.41।।
text_kannada:
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತ್ವಮಿಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣ್ಯಾದೌ ನಿಯಮ್ಯ ಭರತರ್ಷಭ |
ಪಾಪ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಜಹಿ ಹ್ಯೇನಂ ಜ್ಞಾನವಿಜ್ಞಾನನಾಶನಮ್ || ೪೧ ||

తస్మాత్త్వమింద్రియాణ్యాదౌ నియమ్య భరతర్షభ |
పాప్మానం ప్రజహి హ్యేనం జ్ఞానవిజ్ఞాననాశనమ్ || ౪౧ ||
transliteration:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣhabha
pāpmānaṁ prajahi hyenaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśhanam
translation_english: Therefore, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, after first controlling the organs, completely renounce this one which is sinful and a destroyer of learning and wisdom.
translation_kannada: ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಭರತಶ್ರೇಷ್ಠನೇ, ಮೊದಲು ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳನ್ನು ಹತೋಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಂಡು, ಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನೂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನೂ ನಾಶಮಾಡುವ ಈ ಪಾಪಿಯನ್ನು ಕೊಂದುಹಾಕು.
translation_telugu: అందువలన భరత కుల శ్రేష్టుడా;ముందుగానీవు ఇంద్రియాలని నిగ్రహించి,జ్ఞాన విజ్ఞానాలను నాశనం చేసే పాపిష్టి కామాన్ని నిర్మూలించు.
context_english: tasmāt—therefore; tvam—you; indriyāṇi—senses; ādau—in the very beginning; niyamya—having controlled; bharata-ṛiṣhabha—Arjun, the best of the Bharatas; pāpmānam—the sinful; prajahi—slay; hi—certainly; enam—this; jñāna—knowledge; vijñāna—realization; nāśhanam—the destroyer
commentary_english: Jnana is knowledge obtained through the study of scriptures. This is indirect knowledge or Paroksha Jnana. Vijnana is direct knowledge or personal experience or Anubhava through Selfrealisation or Aparoksha Jnana. Control the senses first and then kill desire.

text:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।

मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः।।3.42।।
text_kannada:
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಪರಾಣ್ಯಾಹುರಿಂದ್ರಿಯೇಭ್ಯಃ ಪರಂ ಮನಃ |
ಮನಸಸ್ತು ಪರಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ಯೋ ಬುದ್ಧೇಃ ಪರತಸ್ತು ಸಃ || ೪೨ ||
text_telugu:
ఇంద్రియాణి పరాణ్యాహురింద్రియేభ్యః పరం మనః |
మనసస్తు పరా బుద్ధిర్యో బుద్ధేః పరతస్తు సః || ౪౨ ||
transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ
translation_english: They say that the organs are superior to the gross body; the mind is superior to the organs; and the intellect is superior to the mind. However, He is superior to the intellect.
translation_kannada: ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳು ದೇಹಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಮೇಲಿನವು ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಮನಸ್ಸು ಮೇಲಿನದು, ಮನಸ್ಸಿಗಿಂತ ಬುದ್ಧಿ ಮೇಲಿನದು; ಬುದ್ಧಿಗಿಂತಲೂ ಮೇಲಿರುವವನು ಆತ್ಮ.
translation_telugu: ఇంద్రియాలు గొప్పవని చెబుతారు.ఇంద్రియాలకన్నా అధికమైనది మనస్సు.మనస్సు కన్నాగొప్పది బుద్ధి,బుద్ధి కంటే శ్రేష్టమైనది ఆత్మ.
context_english: indriyāṇi—senses; parāṇi—superior; āhuḥ—are said; indriyebhyaḥ—than the senses; param—superior; manaḥ—the mind; manasaḥ—than the mind; tu—but; parā—superior; buddhiḥ—intellect; yaḥ—who; buddheḥ—than the intellect; parataḥ—more superior; tu—but; saḥ—that (soul)
commentary_english: When compared with the physical body which is gross? external and limited? the senses are certainly superior as they are more subtle? internal and have a wider range of activity. The mind is superior to the senses? as the senses cannot do anything independently without the help of the mind. The mind can perform the functions of the five senses. The intellect is superior to the mind because it is endowed with the faculty of discrimination. When the mind is in a state of doubt? the intellect comes to its resuce. The Self? the Witness? is superior even to the intellect? as the intellect borrows its light from the Self.

text:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।

जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।
text_kannada:
ಏವಂ ಬುದ್ಧೇಃ ಪರಂ ಬುದ್ಧ್ವಾ ಸಂಸ್ತಭ್ಯಾತ್ಮಾನಮಾತ್ಮನಾ |

translation_telugu: మహాబాహుడా ఇలా ఆత్మను బుద్ధికన్నా ఎక్కువైన దానిగా తెలుసుకొని నిన్ను నీవు నిగ్రహించుకొని,కామరూపి అయిన శత్రువుని జయించు.

commentary_english: Restrain the lower self by the higher Self. Subdue the lower mind by the higher mind. text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।

विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्।।4.1।।

translation_english: The Blessed Lord said, "I imparted this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan, who then taught it to Manu, who in turn transmitted it to Iksavaku.

स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप।।4.2।।
text_kannada:
ಏವಂ ಪರಂಪರಾಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಮಿಮಂ ರಾಜರ್ಷಯೋ ವಿದುಃ |

ఏవం పరంపరాప్రాప్తమిమం రాజర్షయో విదుః |

transliteration:

text:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।

भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्।।4.3।।
text_kannada:
ಸ ಏವಾಯಂ ಮಯಾ ತೇಽದ್ಯ ಯೋಗಃ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಃ ಪುರಾತನಃ |
ಭಕ್ತೋಽಸಿ ಮೇ ಸಖಾ ಚೇತಿ ರಹಸ್ಯಂ ಹ್ಯೇತದುತ್ತಮಮ್ || ೩ ||

స ఏవాయం మయా తేఽద్య యోగః ప్రోక్తః పురాతనః |
భక్తోఽసి మే సఖా చేతి రహస్యం హ్యేతదుత్తమమ్ || ౩ ||

sa evāyaṁ mayā te ’dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto ’si me sakhā cheti rahasyaṁ hyetad uttamam

text:
अर्जुन उवाच

अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।

कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति।।4.4।।
text_kannada:
ಅರ್ಜುನ ಉವಾಚ |
ಅಪರಂ ಭವತೋ ಜನ್ಮ ಪರಂ ಜನ್ಮ ವಿವಸ್ವತಃ |
ಕಥಮೇತದ್ವಿಜಾನೀಯಾಂ ತ್ವಮಾದೌ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತವಾನಿತಿ || ೪ ||
text_telugu:
అర్జున ఉవాచ |
అపరం భవతో జన్మ పరం జన్మ వివస్వతః |
కథమేతద్విజానీయాం త్వమాదౌ ప్రోక్తవానితి || ౪ ||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ
katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti
translation_english: Arjuna said, "Your birth was later, whereas Vivasvan's birth was earlier. How am I to understand that You instructed him in the beginning?"
translation_kannada: ಅರ್ಜುನನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ನಿನ್ನ ಜನ್ಮ ಈಚಿನದು, ವಿವಸ್ವಂತನ ಜನ್ಮ ಬಹಳ ಹಿಂದಿನದು. ಹಾಗಿರುವಾಗ ನೀನೇ ಮೊದಲು ಇದನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿದೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನಾನು ಹೇಗೆ ತಿಳಿಯಲಿ?
translation_telugu: అర్జునుడు ఇలా అడిగాడు:- నీ జన్మ ఇటీవలది.సూర్యుని జన్మ ఎంతో ముందున్నది.నీవు సూర్యునికి ఉపదేశించావని అన్నావు.దీనిని ఎలా అర్ధం చేసుకోవాలి?
context_english: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; aparam—later; bhavataḥ—your; janma—birth; param—prior; janma—birth; vivasvataḥ—Vivasvan, the sun-god; katham—how; etat—this; vijānīyām—am I to understand; tvam—you; ādau—in the beginning; proktavān—taught; iti—thus
commentary_english: Thy birth took place later in the hourse of Vasudeva Vivasvan or Vivasvat (the Sun) was born earlier in the beginning of evolution. How am I to believe that Thou taughtest this Yoga in the beginning to Vivasvan? and that Thou? the selfsame person? hast now taught it to me I am not able to reconcile this. Be kind enought to enlighten me? O my Lord.

text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।

तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप।।4.5।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರೀ ಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ |
ಬಹೂನಿ ಮೇ ವ್ಯತೀತಾನಿ ಜನ್ಮಾನಿ ತವ ಚಾರ್ಜುನ |
ತಾನ್ಯಹಂ ವೇದ ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ನ ತ್ವಂ ವೇತ್ಥ ಪರಂತಪ || ೫ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ |
బహూని మే వ్యతీతాని జన్మాని తవ చార్జున |
తాన్యహం వేద సర్వాణి న త్వం వేత్థ పరంతప || ౫ ||
transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava chārjuna
tānyahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa
translation_english: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, many lives of Mine have passed, and so have yours. I know them all, but you do not know, O scorcher of enemies!"
translation_kannada: ಶ್ರೀಭಗವಂತನು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ಅರ್ಜುನಾ, ನನಗೂ ನಿನಗೂ ಅನೇಕ ಜನ್ಮಗಳು ಕಳೆದಿವೆ. ಶತ್ರುಗಳನ್ನು ತಪಿಸುವವನೇ, ಅವೆಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ನಾನು ಬಲ್ಲೆ, ನೀನು ತಿಳಿಯೆ.
translation_telugu: శ్రీ కృష్ణభగవానుడు ఇలా పలికాడు:- అర్జునా! నాకూ నీకూ కూడా ఎన్నో జన్మలు గడిచిపోయాయి.నేను వాటన్నిటిని ఎరుగుదును.నీవు ఎరుగవు.
context_english: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—the Supreme Lord said; bahūni—many; me—of mine; vyatītāni—have passed; janmāni—births; tava—of yours; cha—and; arjuna—Arjun; tāni—them; aham—I; veda—know; sarvāṇi—all; na—not; tvam—you; vettha—know; parantapa—Arjun, the scorcher of foes
commentary_english: You have no intuitional knowledge. The eye of wisdom has not been opened in you on account of your past actions. So your power of vision is limited and therefore you do not know your previous births. But I know them because I am omniscient.

text:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।

प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया।।4.6।।
text_kannada:
ಅಜೋಽಪಿ ಸನ್ನವ್ಯಯಾತ್ಮಾ ಭೂತಾನಾಮೀಶ್ವರೋಽಪಿ ಸನ್ |
ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಂ ಸ್ವಾಮಧಿಷ್ಠಾಯ ಸಂಭವಾಮ್ಯಾತ್ಮಮಾಯಯಾ || ೬ ||

అజోఽపి సన్నవ్యయాత్మా భూతానామీశ్వరోఽపి సన్ |
ప్రకృతిం స్వామధిష్ఠాయ సంభవామ్యాత్మమాయయా || ౬ ||
transliteration:
ajo ’pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānām īśhvaro ’pi san
prakṛitiṁ svām adhiṣhṭhāya sambhavāmyātma-māyayā
translation_english: Though I am birthless and undecaying by nature, and the Lord of beings, yet by subjugating My Prakriti, I take birth through My own Maya.
translation_kannada: ನಾನು ಹುಟ್ಟಿಲ್ಲದವನೂ ನಾಶವಿಲ್ಲದ ಸ್ವರೂಪವುಳ್ಳವನೂ ಎಲ್ಲ ಜೀವಿಗಳ ಒಡೆಯನೂ ಆಗಿದ್ದರೂ, ನನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯನ್ನು ಆಶ್ರಯಿಸಿ ನನ್ನ ಮಾಯೆಯಿಂದ ಅವತರಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ.
translation_telugu: జన్మ లేనివాడినీ,అవ్యయుడినీ,జీవులందరికి అధిపతినైనా,నాప్రకృతిని అధిరోహించి నామాయవలన జన్మిస్తుంటాను.
context_english: ajaḥ—unborn; api—although; san—being so; avyaya ātmā—Imperishable nature; bhūtānām—of (all) beings; īśhvaraḥ—the Lord; api—although; san—being; prakṛitim—nature; svām—of myself; adhiṣhṭhāya—situated; sambhavāmi—I manifest; ātma-māyayā—by my Yogmaya power
commentary_english: Man is bound by Karma. So he takes birth. He is under the clutches of Nature. He,is deluded by the three alities of Nature whereas the Lord has Maya under His perfect control. He rules over Nature? and so He is not under the thraldom of the alities o Nature. He appears to be born and embodied through His own Maya or illusory power? but is not so in reality. His embodiment is ? as a matter of fact? apparent? It cannot affect in the least His true divine nature. (Cf.IX.8).
